explanations.C: Using the entire **VPC CIDR block** (e.g., 10.0.0.0/16) as the source is too permissive. It allows *any* instance in the entire VPC to access the target, even instances that are not part of the communicating application tier. This violates the principle of least privilege.
explanations.D: Using the **subnet CIDR block** (e.g., 10.0.1.0/24) is also too permissive. While it is more restrictive than the VPC CIDR, it still allows every instance within that specific subnet to access the target, which violates least privilege if other, unrelated instances share that subnet.
explanations.correct: Referencing the security group ID of a different tier in the security group rules is the AWS best practice for implementing least privilege networking between tiers. It allows communication based on the logical grouping of instances (the application tier) rather than broad, less secure IP ranges (CIDR blocks).

questions.text: A solutions architect is implementing a document review application using an Amazon S3 bucket for storage. The solution must prevent accidental deletion of the documents and ensure that all versions of the documents are available. Users must be able to download, modify, and upload documents. Which combination of actions should be taken to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Enable a read-only bucket ACL.
options.B: Enable versioning on the bucket.
options.C: Attach an IAM policy to the bucket.
options.D: Enable MFA Delete on the bucket.
options.E: Encrypt the bucket using AWS KMS.

explanations.A: Enabling a read-only bucket ACL would prevent users from modifying and uploading documents (PUT/DELETE actions), which contradicts the requirement that users must be able to download, modify, and upload documents.
explanations.B: Enabling **versioning** on the bucket is necessary to meet the requirement to **ensure all versions of the documents are available**. Even when a user 'modifies' or 'deletes' a file, the old version is preserved. A 'delete' operation simply adds a delete marker, which can be easily reverted.
explanations.C: While an IAM policy is required to grant users permission to download, modify, and upload documents, this action alone does not prevent the *accidental deletion* of the bucket or objects, nor does it ensure that *all versions* are available.
explanations.D: Enabling **MFA Delete** on the bucket prevents the accidental or malicious permanent deletion of objects or the suspension of versioning on the bucket, which directly addresses the requirement to **prevent accidental deletion of the documents**. This requires a physical Multi-Factor Authentication device to confirm the deletion request.
explanations.E: Encrypting the bucket using AWS KMS (SSE-KMS) addresses data security and compliance, but it is not directly required to **prevent accidental deletion** or to **ensure all versions of the documents are available**.
explanations.correct: Versioning (B) ensures that every change/deletion is tracked and recoverable, meeting the requirement to have all versions available. MFA Delete (D) provides a high layer of protection against accidental (or malicious) permanent deletion of objects or the versioning state, meeting the requirement to prevent accidental deletion.

questions.text: A company needs to review its AWS Cloud deployment to ensure that its Amazon S3 buckets do not have unauthorized configuration changes. What should a solutions architect do to accomplish this goal?

options.A: Turn on AWS Config with the appropriate rules.
options.B: Turn on AWS Trusted Advisor with the appropriate checks.
options.C: Turn on Amazon Inspector with the appropriate assessment template.
options.D: Turn on Amazon S3 server access logging. Configure Amazon EventBridge (Amazon Cloud Watch Events).

explanations.A: **AWS Config** is the native AWS service designed to record and evaluate configurations of AWS resources. By enabling Config with appropriate **Config Rules** (e.g., `s3-bucket-public-read-prohibited`), a solutions architect can continuously monitor S3 buckets for unauthorized configuration changes, deviations from best practices, or policy violations. This directly meets the requirement.
explanations.B: AWS Trusted Advisor provides checks across five categories (Cost Optimization, Performance, Security, Fault Tolerance, and Service Limits). While it offers recommendations, it is a point-in-time assessment tool and **does not provide continuous, detailed configuration history or automatic remediation** for every configuration change, which is necessary for continuous monitoring.
explanations.C: Amazon Inspector is a security assessment service that focuses on inspecting **EC2 instances and container images** for software vulnerabilities and unintended network exposure. It is not used for monitoring the configuration changes of an Amazon S3 bucket.
explanations.D: Amazon S3 server access logging records **requests made to the S3 bucket** (who accessed what and when). It does not track or evaluate **configuration changes** (like changing a bucket policy or disabling versioning), which is the core requirement of the question.
explanations.correct: AWS Config is the primary service for continuous auditing, compliance assessment, and tracking configuration changes on AWS resources, including S3 buckets. Its rules can automatically check if a configuration remains compliant with defined security standards.

questions.text: A company’s compliance team needs to move its file shares to AWS. The shares run on a Windows Server SMB file share. A self-managed on-premises Active Directory controls access to the files and folders. The company wants to use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server as part of the solution. The company must ensure that the on-premises Active Directory groups restrict access to the FSx for Windows File Server SMB compliance shares, folders, and files after the move to AWS. The company has created an FSx for Windows File Server file system. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Active Directory Connector to connect to the Active Directory. Map the Active Directory groups to IAM groups to restrict access.
options.B: Assign a tag with a Restrict tag key and a Compliance tag value. Map the Active Directory groups to IAM groups to restrict access.
options.C: Create an IAM service-linked role that is linked directly to FSx for Windows File Server to restrict access.
options.D: Join the file system to the Active Directory to restrict access.

explanations.A: AWS Managed Microsoft AD (or AD Connector) is required to use FSx, but access control is still managed by the directory itself, not by mapping AD groups to IAM groups. IAM groups are used for AWS API permissions, not for file and folder permissions on the SMB share.
explanations.B: AWS resource tagging is used for resource organization and cost allocation. It cannot be used to control file-level access via the Server Message Block (SMB) protocol for Windows shares.
explanations.C: IAM service-linked roles are used to delegate permission to AWS services to perform actions on your behalf (e.g., FSx creating EC2 instances). They do not govern file and folder access permissions for end-users accessing an SMB share.
explanations.D: Amazon FSx for Windows File Server is designed to provide fully managed, highly available SMB file storage that integrates natively with Microsoft Active Directory (AD). To control access using on-premises AD groups and leverage existing Windows Access Control Lists (ACLs), the FSx file system **must be joined to the Active Directory domain**. This allows users and groups authenticated by the AD to access the share and restricts access based on their existing AD permissions.
explanations.correct: The fundamental requirement for Amazon FSx for Windows File Server to honor on-premises Active Directory permissions (groups, users, and ACLs) is for the file system to be joined to that specific Active Directory domain. This allows Windows-native authentication and authorization to control SMB access at the share, folder, and file level.

questions.text:
A solutions architect needs to design a highly available application consisting of web, application, and database tiers. HTTPS content delivery should be as close to the edge as possible, with the least delivery time.
Which solution meets these requirements and is MOST secure?

options.A: Configure a public Application Load Balancer (ALB) with multiple redundant Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets. Configure Amazon CloudFront to deliver HTTPS content using the public ALB as the origin.
options.B: Configure a public Application Load Balancer with multiple redundant Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets. Configure Amazon CloudFront to deliver HTTPS content using the EC2 instances as the origin.
options.C: Configure a public Application Load Balancer (ALB) with multiple redundant Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets. Configure Amazon CloudFront to deliver HTTPS content using the public ALB as the origin.
options.D: Configure a public Application Load Balancer with multiple redundant Amazon EC2 instances in public subnets. Configure Amazon CloudFront to deliver HTTPS content using the EC2 instances as the origin.

explanations.A: This option is not MOST secure. Placing the EC2 instances (which contain the application logic) in public subnets makes them directly accessible from the internet, violating the security best practice of placing application servers in private subnets behind a load balancer. Additionally, using an ALB is preferred over direct EC2 access for an origin.
explanations.B: This option is not ideal. While placing EC2 instances in private subnets is good practice, using the **EC2 instance IP address** directly as the CloudFront origin is not highly available. CloudFront should point to a highly available, redundant endpoint like an Application Load Balancer (ALB), which can distribute traffic across the redundant EC2 instances and handle health checks.
explanations.C: This solution meets all requirements: **Highly Available** (redundant EC2 instances, ALB across multiple AZs, CloudFront), **Low Latency** (CloudFront delivers content from the edge), and **MOST Secure**. Security best practice dictates that the application EC2 instances must reside in **private subnets**, accessible only by the public-facing service (the ALB). The ALB provides the single, highly available, and secure endpoint (origin) that CloudFront is configured to use.
explanations.D: This option is not MOST secure. Placing EC2 instances in **public subnets** violates the principle of defense-in-depth and exposes the application servers directly to the internet, making them susceptible to direct attacks. Furthermore, using an ALB as the origin is better for high availability than pointing CloudFront directly to a single EC2 instance's IP address.
explanations.correct: The most secure and highly available design uses Amazon CloudFront for edge delivery, points it to a highly available **Application Load Balancer (ALB)**, and protects the underlying application servers by placing the **EC2 instances in private subnets**.

questions.text: A company is launching a new application and will display application metrics on an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard. The company's product manager needs to access this dashboard periodically. The product manager does not have an AWS account. A solutions architect must provide access to the product manager by following the principle of least privilege. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Share the dashboard from the CloudWatch console. Enter the product manager's email address, and complete the sharing steps. Provide a shareable link for the dashboard to the product manager.
options.B: Create an IAM user specifically for the product manager. Attach the CloudWatchReadOnlyAccess AWS managed policy to the user. Share the new login credentials with the product manager. Share the browser URL of the correct dashboard with the product manager.
options.C: Create an IAM user for the company's employees. Attach the ViewOnlyAccess AWS managed policy to the IAM user. Share the new login credentials with the product manager. Ask the product manager to navigate to the CloudWatch console and locate the dashboard by name in the Dashboards section.
options.D: Deploy a bastion server in a public subnet. When the product manager requires access to the dashboard, start the server and share the RDP credentials. On the bastion server, ensure that the browser is configured to open the dashboard URL with cached AWS credentials that have appropriate permissions to view the dashboard.

explanations.A: This is the correct solution. **CloudWatch dashboard sharing** allows users who do not have an AWS account to view a specific dashboard using a secure, temporary, and non-console-based URL. This method adheres to the principle of least privilege because the user is granted access only to the dashboard itself and no other AWS resources. It requires no AWS account or IAM credentials for the product manager, fulfilling the requirement simply and securely.
explanations.B: Creating an IAM user for someone who does not have an AWS account (and is not a technical resource requiring API access) is a security risk and an operational overhead. While `CloudWatchReadOnlyAccess` adheres to least privilege for CloudWatch access, sharing IAM credentials is poor security practice, especially for external or non-technical users. This is not the most appropriate or secure method.
explanations.C: Sharing IAM credentials between multiple employees (creating one user for all) is a severe violation of security best practices as it breaks individual accountability. Furthermore, the product manager does not have an AWS account, and providing shared credentials is fundamentally insecure.
explanations.D: Using a bastion host for viewing a dashboard introduces unnecessary complexity, cost, and operational overhead. A bastion host is used for secure access to private resources (like EC2 instances), not for simple, periodic viewing of a publicly shareable, read-only web dashboard. It is a highly over-engineered solution.
explanations.correct: CloudWatch dashboard sharing is the simplest, most secure, and lowest-friction method for granting read-only access to a dashboard for users who are not part of the organization's AWS account. The shared link provides temporary, anonymous access to the data, satisfying the requirements with minimal overhead and adhering to the principle of least privilege.

references: AWS CloudWatch dashboard sharing is designed to provide read-only access to specific dashboards without requiring AWS credentials or accounts.
AWS SAA Exam Guide D1: Secure access to AWS resources.

questions.text: A company is using a centralized AWS account to store log data in various Amazon S3 buckets. A solutions architect needs to ensure that the data is encrypted at rest before the data is uploaded to the S3 buckets. The data also must be encrypted in transit. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Use client-side encryption to encrypt the data that is being uploaded to the S3 buckets.
options.B: Use server-side encryption to encrypt the data that is being uploaded to the S3 buckets.
options.C: Create bucket policies that require the use of server-side encryption with S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) for S3 uploads.
options.D: Enable the security option to encrypt the S3 buckets through the use of a default AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key.

explanations.A: Client-Side Encryption ensures data is encrypted before leaving the client application. While it meets the 'encrypted at rest' requirement, it requires modification of the client application/process for every log source, which is operationally intensive and doesn't enforce the requirement at the S3 bucket level for all clients.
explanations.B: Server-Side Encryption is the mechanism for encrypting data at rest on S3, but this option is incomplete. To *ensure* (enforce) this encryption for *all* uploads, a bucket policy is required. Without enforcement, a client can still upload unencrypted data.
explanations.C: This is the most secure and operationally sound solution. Using a **bucket policy** with the `s3:x-amz-server-side-encryption` condition key allows the solutions architect to **enforce** that all incoming objects must be uploaded with Server-Side Encryption (SSE-S3, SSE-KMS, or SSE-C). This meets the 'data encrypted at rest' requirement by making it mandatory. Additionally, the requirement for 'encrypted in transit' is a standard security best practice, and all modern SDKs and S3 client connections use HTTPS/TLS by default, ensuring data is encrypted during upload.
explanations.D: Enabling default encryption using SSE-KMS is a good security measure, but it only applies to objects that are uploaded *without* encryption headers. It is safer to use a bucket policy to *reject* any unencrypted uploads explicitly, thereby enforcing the encryption standard for all objects, which is a stronger control than the default encryption feature.
explanations.correct: To *ensure* data is encrypted at rest, the S3 bucket policy must be used to explicitly reject any upload that does not contain the appropriate server-side encryption header (`x-amz-server-side-encryption`). This enforces the encryption requirement for all clients. Data is encrypted in transit by connecting to S3 via HTTPS/TLS, which is the default for most AWS services.

references: AWS S3 Bucket Policies are used to enforce security requirements, such as requiring Server-Side Encryption (SSE-S3 or SSE-KMS) on all uploads.
All communication with Amazon S3 should use the SSL/TLS protocol to ensure data is encrypted in transit.

questions.text:
A company has an application that is backed by an Amazon DynamoDB table. The company’s compliance requirements specify that database backups must be taken every month, must be available for 6 months, and must be retained for 7 years.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an AWS Backup plan to back up the DynamoDB table on the first day of each month. Specify a lifecycle policy that transitions the backup to cold storage after 6 months. Set the retention period for each backup to 7 years.
options.B: Create a DynamoDB on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table on the first day of each month. Transition the backup to Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval after 6 months. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to delete backups that are older than 7 years.
options.C: Use the AWS SDK to develop a script that creates an on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table. Set up an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs the script on the first day of each month. Create a second script that will run on the second day of each month to transition DynamoDB backups that are older than 6 months to cold storage and to delete backups that are older than 7 years.
options.D: Use the AWS CLI to create an on-demand backup of the DynamoDB table. Set up an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs the command on the first day of each month with a cron expression. Specify in the command to transition the backups to cold storage after 6 months and to delete the backups after 7 years.

explanations.A: This is the correct solution and the **MOST operationally efficient and robust** method. **AWS Backup** is a fully managed service designed to centralize and automate data protection across multiple AWS services, including DynamoDB. A single **Backup plan** can define the schedule (monthly), the total **retention period** (7 years for compliance), and a **lifecycle policy** to automatically transition the recovery points to low-cost **cold storage** (after 6 months) for cost optimization. This meets all requirements without custom scripting or manual intervention.
explanations.B: This option is incorrect. DynamoDB on-demand backups (when managed natively by DynamoDB, not AWS Backup) are retained indefinitely until manually deleted and **cannot** be directly transitioned to S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval or managed by S3 Lifecycle policies. Lifecycle management (cold storage tiering and final deletion) for DynamoDB backups is a feature provided exclusively by **AWS Backup**.
explanations.C: This solution relies on **custom scripts** and AWS Lambda/EventBridge for scheduling, retention, and lifecycle management. While technically possible, it is not the **most operationally efficient** way in AWS, as it requires writing, maintaining, and debugging code for a feature already provided by the fully managed **AWS Backup** service.
explanations.D: This option incorrectly assumes that the AWS CLI or the DynamoDB `create-backup` API command can specify lifecycle policies (cold storage transition and deletion). These lifecycle features are managed at the **AWS Backup Plan/Rule** level, not within the individual `create-backup` command. Furthermore, relying on EventBridge and a CLI command for long-term compliance is less centralized and auditable than using AWS Backup.
explanations.correct: AWS Backup is the recommended, fully managed service for meeting long-term, scheduled backup and compliance requirements for DynamoDB. It allows the creation of a single plan to define the schedule (monthly backup), the long retention period (7 years), and the lifecycle policy (transition to cold storage after 6 months) to maximize cost savings for long-term archives.

questions.text:
A company is migrating applications to AWS. The applications are deployed in different accounts. The company manages the accounts centrally by using AWS Organizations. The company's security team needs a single sign-on (SSO) solution across all the company's accounts. The company must continue managing the users and groups in its on-premises self-managed Microsoft Active Directory.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Enable AWS Single Sign-On (AWS SSO) from the AWS SSO console. Create a one-way forest trust or a one-way domain trust to connect the company's self-managed Microsoft Active Directory with AWS SSO by using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory.
options.B: Enable AWS Single Sign-On (AWS SSO) from the AWS SSO console. Create a two-way forest trust to connect the company's self-managed Microsoft Active Directory with AWS SSO by using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory.
options.C: Use AWS Directory Service. Create a two-way trust relationship with the company's self-managed Microsoft Active Directory.
options.D: Deploy an identity provider (IdP) on premises. Enable AWS Single Sign-On (AWS SSO) from the AWS SSO console.

explanations.A: This is the correct solution. **AWS SSO** (now known as AWS IAM Identity Center) is the service designed for centralizing SSO access across multiple accounts in **AWS Organizations**. To connect an on-premises, self-managed Active Directory for user and group synchronization and authentication, you must use **AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory** (Managed AD). This managed AD then uses a **one-way trust** relationship (specifically a one-way **outbound** trust from the Managed AD to the on-premises AD) to look up users and groups in the on-premises directory without the need to replicate or migrate them. The one-way trust is sufficient and is the principle of least privilege required to allow AWS to read identity information for SSO, while preventing the on-premises AD from reading resources in the AWS Managed AD domain.
explanations.B: A **two-way forest trust** allows principals in both domains to be granted access to resources in the other domain. For the purpose of using the on-premises AD as the source of truth for SSO in AWS, a one-way trust is sufficient and more secure (least privilege). The two-way trust is typically used when you need to access resources within the Managed AD from your on-premises AD, which is not required here.
explanations.C: Simply creating a trust relationship with AWS Directory Service alone does not provide the **Single Sign-On (SSO) solution across all accounts** requirement. You must enable and configure **AWS SSO (IAM Identity Center)**, which orchestrates the access across the AWS Organization using the directory service as the identity source. Directory Service is the component, but IAM Identity Center is the full solution.
explanations.D: You do not need to deploy a separate IdP on-premises if you leverage the integrated solution. AWS IAM Identity Center integrates directly with your on-premises Active Directory via the AWS Directory Service, which acts as the intermediary IdP, simplifying the architecture and management compared to managing a separate component like an ADFS server on-premises.
explanations.correct: The most secure and efficient way to achieve centralized SSO across an AWS Organization while keeping users and groups managed on-premises is to use **AWS IAM Identity Center (formerly AWS SSO)**, linked to **AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory**, which establishes a **one-way trust** to the self-managed on-premises AD. The one-way trust (specifically, the managed directory trusts the on-premises directory) meets the requirement of using the on-premises AD as the source of truth with the principle of least privilege.
explanations.diagram_query: AWS IAM Identity Center and one-way trust with On-Premises Active Directory

questions.text: A company runs a web application that is deployed on Amazon EC2 instances in the private subnet of a VPC. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) that extends across the public subnets directs web traffic to the EC2 instances. The company wants to implement new security measures to restrict inbound traffic from the ALB to the EC2 instances while preventing access from any other source inside or outside the private subnet of the EC2 instances. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure a route in a route table to direct traffic from the internet to the private IP addresses of the EC2 instances.
options.B: Configure the security group for the EC2 instances to only allow traffic that comes from the security group for the ALB.
options.C: Move the EC2 instances into the public subnet. Give the EC2 instances a set of Elastic IP addresses.
options.D: Configure the security group for the ALB to allow any TCP traffic on any port.

explanations.A: Configuring a route in a route table to direct traffic from the internet to the private IP addresses is incorrect and highly insecure. Routes only define *where* traffic is sent, not *what* traffic is allowed. Furthermore, the private subnet is designed to prevent direct internet access, so directing internet traffic to private IPs via routing would break the architecture and expose the instances directly.
explanations.B: This is the most secure and correct method for restricting inbound traffic to backend instances in a private subnet that are behind a load balancer.  By referencing the **ALB's security group** in the **EC2 instance's security group** (as the source), the EC2 instance will only accept traffic that has passed through the ALB. The private IP addresses of the ALB nodes, which are dynamic, are handled automatically by this security group reference, and no traffic from other sources (even other private instances or the public internet) can directly reach the EC2 instances on the allowed ports.
explanations.C: Moving EC2 instances into a public subnet, and assigning Elastic IPs, completely defeats the purpose of the private subnet (security and isolation). This makes the web servers directly accessible from the internet, which violates the requirement to restrict access only to the ALB and exposes the servers to a much wider attack surface.
explanations.D: The security group for the **ALB** controls traffic *into* the ALB (e.g., ports 80/443 from 0.0.0.0/0). This option is overly permissive for the ALB (allowing 'any TCP traffic on any port') but, more importantly, it does nothing to restrict traffic *to* the EC2 instances in the private subnet, which is the core requirement of the question.
explanations.correct: Security groups can be configured to use another security group as a source, which is the best practice for chaining trust between components like an ALB and backend EC2 instances. This ensures only traffic originating from the ALB's internal interfaces can reach the EC2 web servers, providing strong isolation from any other source.

questions.text: A company wants to migrate a Windows-based application from on premises to the AWS Cloud. The application has three tiers: an application tier, a business tier, and a database tier with Microsoft SQL Server. The company wants to use specific features of SQL Server such as native backups and Data Quality Services. The company also needs to share files for processing between the tiers. How should a solutions architect design the architecture to meet these requirements?

options.A: Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx File Gateway for file sharing between the tiers.
options.B: Host all three tiers on Amazon EC2 instances. Use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server for file sharing between the tiers.
options.C: Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for file sharing between the tiers.
options.D: Host the application tier and the business tier on Amazon EC2 instances. Host the database tier on Amazon RDS. Use a Provisioned IOPS SSD (io2) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume for file sharing between the tiers.

explanations.A: Hosting all three tiers on EC2 instances is correct because it supports the required **custom SQL Server features** (native backups, Data Quality Services) which are unavailable in Amazon RDS for SQL Server. However, **Amazon FSx File Gateway** is designed to provide on-premises access to cloud storage (S3) and is not intended for high-performance, cloud-native Windows file sharing between EC2 instances.
explanations.B: This is the correct solution.  **1. Compute:** All three tiers (including SQL Server) must be hosted on **Amazon EC2 instances** running Windows. This is necessary because the requirement to use specific, advanced SQL Server features (like native backups and Data Quality Services) is typically not supported by the managed service, Amazon RDS. **2. File Sharing:** **Amazon FSx for Windows File Server** provides a fully managed, highly available file system that is natively compatible with Windows (SMB protocol). This is the best solution for shared file storage between Windows EC2 instances.
explanations.C: Hosting the database on **Amazon RDS** is incorrect because RDS does not support all advanced SQL Server features like native backups, Data Quality Services, or custom installation components. Additionally, **Amazon EFS (Elastic File System)** is a Linux/NFS-based file system and is not the native, high-performance file sharing solution for Windows EC2 instances (which use SMB).
explanations.D: Hosting the database on **Amazon RDS** is incorrect for the reasons mentioned above (lack of custom SQL Server feature support). Furthermore, an **EBS volume** is block storage that can only be attached to a **single** EC2 instance at a time (unless Multi-Attach is used, but this is complex and not the standard file sharing solution). It cannot be easily shared between the application and business tiers for file processing.
explanations.correct: When custom SQL Server features are required, the database must be self-managed on EC2. The Windows environment mandates a native SMB file share for efficient inter-tier processing, which is perfectly provided by the managed, high-performance Amazon FSx for Windows File Server.

questions.text: A company is migrating a Linux-based web server group to AWS. The web servers must access files in a shared file store for some content. The company must not make any changes to the application. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Amazon S3 Standard bucket with access to the web servers.
options.B: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution with an Amazon S3 bucket as the origin.
options.C: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system on all web servers.
options.D: Configure a General Purpose SSD (gp3) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Mount the EBS volume to all web servers.

explanations.A: Amazon S3 is object storage, not a traditional file system. For a Linux application to access S3, it typically requires modifying the application code to use the S3 API or using an S3 FUSE-based file system adapter, which violates the requirement to 'not make any changes to the application.'
explanations.B: Amazon CloudFront is a Content Delivery Network (CDN) used for caching and delivering web content globally. While it improves performance, it does not provide a shared, mutable file system for backend Linux web servers. It is used for *serving* content, not for the *backend access* to the content source.
explanations.C: This is the correct solution.  **Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS)** is a managed, scalable, shared **NFS (Network File System)** file service, which is the native file sharing protocol for Linux. EFS can be simultaneously mounted across thousands of Amazon EC2 instances. Since the application is Linux-based and requires a shared file store without code changes, mounting a standards-compliant NFS share like EFS is the simplest and most compliant approach.
explanations.D: An **Amazon EBS volume** is block storage that can typically be attached to **only one** EC2 instance at a time. While EBS Multi-Attach exists, it is not supported for all instance types and file systems, and it is a complex configuration. EBS is fundamentally designed for single-instance primary storage, not a simple, highly scalable, shared file system across a fleet of web servers.
explanations.correct: Amazon EFS is a managed, highly available NFS file system that can be concurrently mounted and accessed by multiple Linux EC2 instances. This allows the legacy Linux application to access the shared file store using standard POSIX file system commands without requiring any application code changes.

questions.text: A company has an AWS Lambda function that needs read access to an Amazon S3 bucket that is located in the same AWS account. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST secure manner?

options.A: Apply an S3 bucket policy that grants read access to the S3 bucket.
options.B: Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to the S3 bucket.
options.C: Embed an access key and a secret key in the Lambda function’s code to grant the required IAM permissions for read access to the S3 bucket.
options.D: Apply an IAM role to the Lambda function. Apply an IAM policy to the role to grant read access to all S3 buckets in the account.

explanations.A: An S3 bucket policy can be used to grant access, but it is not the **MOST secure** method when an IAM entity (like a Lambda execution role) is available. Using the Lambda function's execution role to grant permissions is the best practice for giving AWS compute services access to other AWS resources within the same account. It keeps the permissions centralized and easier to manage.
explanations.B: This is the **MOST secure** and recommended solution.  AWS Lambda uses an **IAM execution role** to assume permissions when running. By attaching an **IAM policy** to this role that grants *only* the specific `s3:GetObject` (read) permissions to *only* the required S3 bucket, you follow the principle of **least privilege**. This is better than a bucket policy because it manages the permission through the compute service's identity, and it is better than option D because it limits the scope of access.
explanations.C: Embedding static access keys and secret keys in code is an anti-pattern and a major security risk. If the code is compromised or accidentally exposed (e.g., in a public repository), the credentials can be stolen, leading to unauthorized access. AWS recommends using IAM roles for access granted to AWS services.
explanations.D: While applying an IAM role to the Lambda function is correct, granting read access to **all S3 buckets** in the account (using a resource like `arn:aws:s3:::*`) violates the principle of **least privilege**. This is less secure than granting access only to the specific, required bucket, which makes option B the superior choice.
explanations.correct: The best practice for granting permissions to an AWS service (like Lambda) to access another AWS resource (like S3) is to use an IAM execution role with an IAM policy. The policy must follow the principle of least privilege by restricting access to only the specific actions (read access) and only the specific resource (the single S3 bucket).

questions.text: A company has an on-premises volume backup solution that has reached its end of life. The company wants to use AWS as part of a new backup solution and wants to maintain local access to all the data while it is backed up on AWS. The company wants to ensure that the data backed up on AWS is automatically and securely transferred. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Use AWS Snowball to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Configure on-premises systems to mount the Snowball S3 endpoint to provide local access to the data.
options.B: Use AWS Snowball Edge to migrate data out of the on-premises solution to Amazon S3. Use the Snowball Edge file interface to provide on-premises systems with local access to the data.
options.C: Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a cached volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and configure a percentage of data to cache locally. Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.
options.D: Use AWS Storage Gateway and configure a stored volume gateway. Run the Storage Gateway software appliance on premises and map the gateway storage volumes to on-premises storage. Mount the gateway storage volumes to provide local access to the data.

explanations.A: AWS Snowball is a data migration service for moving large amounts of data *to* AWS. It is not designed to be a continuous, long-term, hybrid-cloud backup solution that maintains a local copy of all data and automatically transfers backups to AWS.
explanations.B: AWS Snowball Edge is a compute and storage device for edge locations or large-scale data transfer. While it has local storage and compute capabilities, it is not designed to be a permanent, automated, long-term backup solution where a local copy of *all* data is maintained and synchronized to AWS. It's primarily a tool for migration and edge computing.
explanations.C: The **Cached Volume Gateway** stores all data in Amazon S3, only retaining a frequently accessed subset of data locally on premises (cache). This does **not** meet the requirement to *maintain local access to **all** the data* on premises.
explanations.D: The **Stored Volume Gateway** stores the entire primary copy of data locally (on premises) and asynchronously backs up the data as point-in-time snapshots to Amazon S3 (using EBS snapshots). This design meets all requirements: it provides an on-premises backup, maintains local access to **all** the data, and automatically and securely transfers snapshots to AWS.
explanations.correct: The Stored Volume Gateway configuration of AWS Storage Gateway is specifically designed for this use case. It stores all data on-premises (on your local storage infrastructure) for low-latency access and takes point-in-time backups (snapshots) of that data, which are then asynchronously and securely uploaded to AWS as EBS snapshots in S3, meeting the requirement for automated cloud backup and full local access.

questions.text: An application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances needs to access an Amazon S3 bucket. Traffic must not traverse the internet. How should a solutions architect configure access to meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a private hosted zone by using Amazon Route 53.
options.B: Set up a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the VPC.
options.C: Configure the EC2 instances to use a NAT gateway to access the S3 bucket.
options.D: Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the VPC and the S3 bucket.

explanations.A: A private hosted zone with Amazon Route 53 provides private DNS resolution for AWS services but does not inherently prevent traffic from traversing the public internet. It is not the mechanism used to keep S3 traffic within the AWS network.
explanations.B: Setting up a **gateway VPC endpoint** for Amazon S3 allows EC2 instances in the VPC to connect to S3 privately using the AWS internal network, preventing traffic from traversing the public internet. This directly meets the requirement.
explanations.C: A NAT gateway allows instances in a private subnet to connect to the internet or other AWS services (like S3) over the public S3 endpoints, but it still involves traffic leaving the private VPC network and traversing the internet. This violates the requirement that traffic must *not* traverse the internet.
explanations.D: An AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection is used to connect an on-premises network to an AWS VPC. This is irrelevant for connecting an EC2 instance *within* the VPC to an Amazon S3 bucket, which is an AWS service.
explanations.correct: The Gateway VPC Endpoint is the correct AWS service designed to allow instances within a VPC to access S3 (and DynamoDB) using the private AWS network, ensuring the traffic does not traverse the internet and providing secure, high-performance connectivity.

questions.text: An ecommerce company stores terabytes of customer data in the AWS Cloud. The data contains personally identifiable information (PII). The company wants to use the data in three applications. Only one of the applications needs to process the PII. The PII must be removed before the other two applications process the data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Store the data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Create a proxy application layer to intercept and process the data that each application requests.
options.B: Store the data in an Amazon S3 bucket. Process and transform the data by using S3 Object Lambda before returning the data to the requesting application.
options.C: Process the data and store the transformed data in three separate Amazon S3 buckets so that each application has its own custom dataset. Point each application to its respective S3 bucket.
options.D: Process the data and store the transformed data in three separate Amazon DynamoDB tables so that each application has its own custom dataset. Point each application to its respective DynamoDB table.

explanations.A: Creating a custom proxy application layer introduces significant operational overhead (maintaining, scaling, and patching the proxy application) and adds latency. This violates the requirement for the LEAST operational overhead.
explanations.B: **S3 Object Lambda** is a serverless, purpose-built feature that allows you to process data retrieved from S3 with a custom AWS Lambda function before returning it to the requester. This means the original PII data remains secure in S3, and the Lambda function can automatically mask, redact, or transform the PII *only* for the two applications that do not need it, with minimal code and no infrastructure to manage.
explanations.C: This solution involves creating two new, transformed datasets (one with PII and two without) and storing them in separate S3 buckets. While it works, it leads to data duplication and requires an ongoing ETL job (data processing) to maintain consistency between the original data and the two new datasets, increasing operational overhead compared to a real-time transformation solution.
explanations.D: This solution involves creating two new, transformed datasets (one with PII and two without) and storing them in separate DynamoDB tables. Similar to option C, this introduces data duplication and requires an ongoing ETL/replication process to maintain consistency, which has higher operational overhead than a real-time, serverless transformation mechanism like S3 Object Lambda.
explanations.correct: S3 Object Lambda is a serverless feature that intercepts standard S3 GET requests and executes an AWS Lambda function to transform the data *in real-time* before returning it to the application. This approach avoids data duplication, eliminates the need to manage infrastructure (no EC2 instances, proxies, or ETL pipelines), and ensures that the sensitive PII is only shared with the authorized application, thereby providing the LEAST operational overhead.

questions.text: A development team has launched a new application that is hosted on Amazon EC2 instances inside a development VPC. A solutions architect needs to create a new VPC in the same account. The new VPC will be peered with the development VPC. The VPC CIDR block for the development VPC is 192.168.0.0/24. The solutions architect needs to create a CIDR block for the new VPC. The CIDR block must be valid for a VPC peering connection to the development VPC. What is the SMALLEST CIDR block that meets these requirements?

explanations.A: A /32 CIDR block only contains a single IP address (10.0.1.0). This is far too small for a VPC that is intended to host EC2 instances and would not be considered a valid VPC CIDR block. AWS requires a netmask between /16 and /28 for VPCs.
explanations.B: This CIDR block (192.168.0.0/24) is identical to the existing development VPC's CIDR block. VPCs that are being peered must have non-overlapping CIDR blocks. This option would cause an invalid peering connection.
explanations.C: A /32 CIDR block only contains a single IP address (192.168.1.0). This is too small for a VPC and does not meet the requirements for a valid VPC CIDR block (must be between /16 and /28). Additionally, while it is technically a non-overlapping IP address, it is not a valid VPC range.
explanations.D: The CIDR block **10.0.1.0/24** is a valid size for a VPC (a /24 block provides 256 addresses, which is within the /16 to /28 range). Critically, it does not overlap with the development VPC's CIDR block of 192.168.0.0/24, making it a valid option for a VPC peering connection. It is the smallest and most practical VPC CIDR block option provided that also satisfies the non-overlapping requirement.
explanations.correct: VPC peering connections require that the CIDR blocks of the two VPCs do not overlap. The development VPC uses 192.168.0.0/24. Option D, **10.0.1.0/24**, is a valid VPC size and does not overlap with the existing VPC. Options A and C are too small (/32) to be valid VPC CIDRs, and Option B overlaps.

questions.text: A company uses AWS Organizations to manage multiple AWS accounts for different departments. The management account has an Amazon S3 bucket that contains project reports. The company wants to limit access to this S3 bucket to only users of accounts within the organization in AWS Organizations. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST amount of operational overhead?

options.A: Add the aws:PrincipalOrgID global condition key with a reference to the organization ID to the S3 bucket policy.
options.B: Create an organizational unit (OU) for each department. Add the aws:PrincipalOrgPaths global condition key to the S3 bucket policy.
options.C: Use AWS CloudTrail to monitor the CreateAccount, InviteAccountToOrganization, LeaveOrganization, and RemoveAccountFromOrganization events. Update the S3 bucket policy accordingly.
options.D: Tag each user that needs access to the S3 bucket. Add the aws:PrincipalTag global condition key to the S3 bucket policy.

explanations.A: The **aws:PrincipalOrgID** global condition key is specifically designed to restrict access to resources (like an S3 bucket) only to principals (IAM users/roles) that belong to accounts within a specified AWS Organization. This requires a simple, single modification to the S3 bucket policy and automatically applies the restriction to all current and future accounts in the organization, making it the solution with the LEAST operational overhead.
explanations.B: The `aws:PrincipalOrgPaths` condition key is used to restrict access based on the Organizational Unit (OU) path. While this is a valid way to control access within an organization, it requires creating OUs and maintaining the path logic, which is more complex and has higher operational overhead than simply using the organization ID.
explanations.C: Monitoring CloudTrail events and manually updating the S3 bucket policy every time an account is added or removed introduces significant operational overhead, is prone to human error, and creates an availability gap (the policy is not updated instantly). This is not an automated or low-overhead solution.
explanations.D: Tagging every individual user/role (Principal) and maintaining these tags across multiple accounts is a significant operational burden. The primary goal is to restrict access based on the *account's membership* in the Organization, not on individual user attributes.
explanations.correct: The `aws:PrincipalOrgID` condition key is the simplest and most scalable way to centrally enforce access restrictions based on an account's membership within a specified AWS Organization. You only need to know the Organization ID and update one policy, which is significantly less operational overhead than the alternatives.

questions.text: An ecommerce company has noticed performance degradation of its Amazon RDS based web application. The performance degradation is attributed to an increase in the number of read-only SQL queries triggered by business analysts. A solutions architect needs to solve the problem with minimal changes to the existing web application. What should the solutions architect recommend?

options.A: Export the data to Amazon DynamoDB and have the business analysts run their queries.
options.B: Load the data into Amazon ElastiCache and have the business analysts run their queries.
options.C: Create a read replica of the primary database and have the business analysts run their queries.
options.D: Copy the data into an Amazon Redshift cluster and have the business analysts run their queries

explanations.A: Amazon DynamoDB is a NoSQL database. Migrating the data and forcing business analysts to use a different query language (non-SQL) is a significant change and does not address the requirement of minimal changes while still supporting the analytical queries.
explanations.B: Amazon ElastiCache is an in-memory caching service, typically used to cache *specific*, frequently accessed key-value pairs to speed up application reads. It is not designed to support complex, ad-hoc, full-table analytical SQL queries typically run by business analysts, which would quickly exhaust the cache memory.
explanations.C: This is the most effective and minimal-change solution. **Amazon RDS Read Replicas** provide an asynchronous copy of the primary database. By directing the read-intensive analytical queries from the business analysts to the Read Replica, the read load is entirely offloaded from the primary instance, which hosts the web application. This isolates the analytical workload and resolves the performance degradation on the primary database with **minimal change** to the existing web application (which continues to use the primary database).
explanations.D: Amazon Redshift is a petabyte-scale data warehouse optimized for complex analytical queries on vast datasets. While it is excellent for analytical queries, copying the data there requires a separate ETL/ELT pipeline and a major change in the overall data architecture and querying mechanism for analysts. This is not the solution with the *minimal changes* to the *existing* system for simply offloading analytical reads.
explanations.correct: Amazon RDS Read Replicas are specifically designed to improve read performance and scalability for RDS databases. By creating a replica, the high volume of read-only analytical queries from the business analysts can be directed there, isolating the workload from the transactional primary database used by the ecommerce application and solving the performance degradation with minimal architectural changes.

references: RDS Read Replicas are the standard, simplest mechanism to offload read traffic from the primary instance in an RDS environment.
AWS SAA Exam Guide D2: Designing highly available and scalable relational data stores.

questions.text:
A rapidly growing ecommerce company is running its workloads in a single AWS Region. A solutions architect must create a disaster recovery (DR) strategy that includes a different AWS Region. The company wants its database to be up to date in the DR Region with the least possible latency. The remaining infrastructure in the DR Region needs to run at reduced capacity and must be able to scale up if necessary.
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LOWEST recovery time objective (RTO)?

options.A: Use an Amazon Aurora global database with a pilot light deployment.
options.B: Use an Amazon Aurora global database with a warm standby deployment.
options.C: Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance with a pilot light deployment.
options.D: Use an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance with a warm standby deployment.

explanations.A: A **pilot light** deployment is characterized by running minimal infrastructure (only the core components, like the database) in the DR region, which perfectly matches the requirement for running the remaining infrastructure at **reduced capacity**. However, the **warm standby** strategy (Option B) has a lower RTO because more infrastructure is already running and configured, leading to faster switchover than the pilot light (which requires launching resources). Thus, pilot light does not offer the LOWEST RTO.
explanations.B: This is the correct solution. A **warm standby** deployment involves maintaining a minimal, but ready-to-scale, version of the entire application in the DR region, which aligns with running the remaining infrastructure at **reduced capacity** and being able to **scale up if necessary**. Warm standby offers a **lower RTO** than pilot light or backup-and-restore, as the infrastructure is mostly running. **Amazon Aurora Global Database** provides fast, low-latency, cross-region replication (typically less than 1 second lag), ensuring the database is **up to date with the least possible latency** (lowest RPO for the DB) and allowing for a fast failover (lowest RTO overall).
explanations.C: **Multi-AZ** is a high availability strategy *within a single region* and does not protect against a regional disaster, which is explicitly required in the question (DR strategy that includes a **different AWS Region**). This option fails the cross-region DR requirement. Furthermore, a pilot light RTO is higher than a warm standby RTO.
explanations.D: **Multi-AZ** is a high availability strategy *within a single region* and does not protect against a regional disaster, which is explicitly required in the question (DR strategy that includes a **different AWS Region**). This option fails the cross-region DR requirement. While warm standby offers a low RTO, the database solution must be cross-regional.
explanations.correct: The combination of **Warm Standby** (for the application infrastructure) and **Aurora Global Database** (for the data layer) meets all requirements with the lowest RTO. Warm Standby has a low RTO because infrastructure is mostly provisioned. Aurora Global Database ensures the lowest possible cross-region database replication latency (lowest RPO for the DB) and supports a fast regional failover, which contributes to the lowest overall RTO.

questions.text:
A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances. The company needs to implement a disaster recovery (DR) solution for the application. The DR solution needs to have a recovery time objective (RTO) of less than 4 hours. The DR solution also needs to use the fewest possible AWS resources during normal operations.
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

options.A: Create Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) to back up the EC2 instances. Copy the AMIs to a secondary AWS Region. Automate infrastructure deployment in the secondary Region by using AWS Lambda and custom scripts.
options.B: Create Amazon Machine Images (AMIs) to back up the EC2 instances. Copy the AMIs to a secondary AWS Region. Automate infrastructure deployment in the secondary Region by using AWS CloudFormation.
options.C: Launch EC2 instances in a secondary AWS Region. Keep the EC2 instances in the secondary Region active at all times.
options.D: Launch EC2 instances in a secondary Availability Zone. Keep the EC2 instances in the secondary Availability Zone active at all times.

explanations.A: This option uses the correct DR pattern (**Backup and Restore** or **Pilot Light**) by leveraging AMIs and cross-region copying, which meets the low resource usage requirement. However, using **AWS Lambda and custom scripts** for complex infrastructure deployment is less operationally efficient, harder to maintain, and less repeatable/auditable than using a dedicated Infrastructure as Code (IaC) tool like CloudFormation.
explanations.B: This is the correct solution. This approach is a **Pilot Light** DR strategy, which meets the requirement of using the **fewest possible AWS resources** during normal operations (only AMIs and potentially minimal database resources). An RTO of **less than 4 hours** is achievable with this strategy because the infrastructure deployment is **automated** using **AWS CloudFormation**. CloudFormation is the most operationally efficient and recommended tool for automating and managing infrastructure deployment across regions (Infrastructure as Code), ensuring a consistent, repeatable, and fast recovery process.
explanations.C: Keeping EC2 instances active at all times in a secondary region is a **Warm Standby** or **Multi-site Active/Active** approach. While it would provide a very low RTO, it directly contradicts the requirement to use the **fewest possible AWS resources** during normal operations, making it more expensive than the Pilot Light strategy.
explanations.D: Launching instances in a secondary **Availability Zone** is a high availability (HA) strategy, not a disaster recovery (DR) strategy for a regional failure. The requirement explicitly mentions a DR solution, which typically implies protection against a regional outage by using a secondary **Region**.
explanations.correct: The combination of the **Pilot Light** strategy (using AMIs to meet the low resource/cost requirement) and **AWS CloudFormation** (the most operationally efficient tool for automating the infrastructure build-out to achieve the sub-4-hour RTO) is the best fit. CloudFormation provides a managed, repeatable, and declarative way to deploy the resources upon failover, minimizing manual intervention and time.

questions.text: A company runs a fleet of web servers using an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. After a routine compliance check, the company sets a standard that requires a recovery point objective (RPO) of less than 1 second for all its production databases. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Enable a Multi-AZ deployment for the DB instance.
options.B: Enable auto scaling for the DB instance in one Availability Zone.
options.C: Configure the DB instance in one Availability Zone, and create multiple read replicas in a separate Availability Zone.
options.D: Configure the DB instance in one Availability Zone, and configure AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) change data capture (CDC) tasks.

explanations.A: The RPO (Recovery Point Objective) defines the maximum allowable amount of data loss measured in time. An RPO of less than 1 second requires near-zero data loss.  RDS Multi-AZ uses **synchronous replication** to a standby instance in a different Availability Zone (AZ). This ensures that the standby is always up to date with the primary instance, effectively guaranteeing an RPO close to zero (less than 1 second) in case of a primary AZ failure, as all committed transactions are copied to the standby.
explanations.B: Auto scaling for an RDS instance primarily handles performance and capacity issues (scaling vertically or horizontally in the case of read replicas). It does not provide the near-zero RPO required for disaster recovery, as the primary instance remains in a single AZ with no synchronous standby.
explanations.C: RDS Read Replicas use **asynchronous replication**. While they are useful for scaling read performance and can be used for disaster recovery, the asynchronous nature means there will inevitably be a replication lag, which could easily be more than 1 second. This violates the RPO requirement.
explanations.D: AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) Change Data Capture (CDC) is designed for migrating databases or for ongoing replication between different database engines (heterogeneous migration). While it provides a form of replication, it is an **asynchronous** process, not designed for the near-zero RPO high availability achieved by RDS Multi-AZ synchronous replication. Furthermore, it is a complex and often unnecessary solution when native RDS features (Multi-AZ) already exist for high availability.
explanations.correct: An RPO of less than 1 second requires a near-zero data loss solution. RDS Multi-AZ deployment uses **synchronous replication** to automatically maintain an up-to-date standby replica in a different AZ, ensuring that all committed transactions are replicated before being acknowledged. This is the only option that meets the strict RPO requirement.

questions.text: A company provides a Voice over Internet Protocol (VoIP) service that uses UDP connections. The service consists of Amazon EC2 instances that run in an Auto Scaling group. The company has deployments across multiple AWS Regions. The company needs to route users to the Region with the lowest latency. The company also needs automated failover between Regions. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and an associated target group. Associate the target group with the Auto Scaling group. Use the NLB as an AWS Global Accelerator endpoint in each Region.
options.B: Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and an associated target group. Associate the target group with the Auto Scaling group. Use the ALB as an AWS Global Accelerator endpoint in each Region.
options.C: Deploy a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and an associated target group. Associate the target group with the Auto Scaling group. Create an Amazon Route 53 latency record that points to aliases for each NLB. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses the latency record as an origin.
options.D: Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and an associated target group. Associate the target group with the Auto Scaling group. Create an Amazon Route 53 weighted record that points to aliases for each ALB. Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses the weighted record as an origin.

explanations.A: This is the correct solution. **1. Protocol Compatibility:** VoIP uses UDP, which is supported by the **Network Load Balancer (NLB)**, but not by the Application Load Balancer (ALB). **2. Low Latency Routing and Failover:** **AWS Global Accelerator (AGA)** is designed specifically to route client traffic to the closest healthy endpoint (lowest latency routing) over the reliable AWS global network backbone, and it provides fast, automatic failover between regional endpoints (NLBs or ALBs). Using the NLB as an endpoint for AGA meets all technical requirements.
explanations.B: The **Application Load Balancer (ALB)** operates at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS) and **does not support the UDP protocol** required for the VoIP service. Therefore, this option is technically unfeasible.
explanations.C: While the **NLB** supports UDP, the use of **Route 53 latency-based routing** relies on DNS caching and is not as fast or as precise as Global Accelerator for real-time traffic like VoIP. More importantly, **CloudFront** is a Content Delivery Network (CDN) for caching static content. It is irrelevant and unnecessary for a dynamic, real-time VoIP service.
explanations.D: This option fails on multiple points: **1.** The **ALB** does not support UDP. **2.** **Route 53 weighted records** are used for traffic distribution based on a set percentage, not for lowest latency routing. **3.** **CloudFront** is a CDN and is not suitable for a dynamic VoIP service.
explanations.correct: The VoIP service requires UDP, which mandates the use of a Network Load Balancer (NLB). AWS Global Accelerator is the premier service for routing non-HTTP traffic to the lowest-latency endpoint globally while providing automatic health checks and failover, making the combination of NLB and AGA the ideal solution.

questions.text: A company is running a critical business application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group and access an Amazon RDS DB instance. The design did not pass an operational review because the EC2 instances and the DB instance are all located in a single Availability Zone. A solutions architect must update the design to use a second Availability Zone. Which solution will make the application highly available?

options.A: Provision a subnet in each Availability Zone. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance with connections to each network.
options.B: Provision two subnets that extend across both Availability Zones. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance with connections to each network.
options.C: Provision a subnet in each Availability Zone. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment.
options.D: Provision a subnet that extends across both Availability Zones. Configure the Auto Scaling group to distribute the EC2 instances across both Availability Zones. Configure the DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment.

explanations.A: This option describes a correct way to set up EC2 high availability (Auto Scaling across AZs with a dedicated subnet in each AZ). However, the description for the DB instance is vague and incomplete ('Configure the DB instance with connections to each network' is not the standard RDS Multi-AZ feature), making it less accurate than option C.
explanations.B: This option is technically incorrect because a single subnet cannot span multiple Availability Zones (AZs) in AWS. Subnets are strictly confined to one AZ. This configuration is not possible.
explanations.C: This is the most accurate and recommended solution for achieving high availability across the application and database layers. Provisioning a subnet per AZ is the correct networking design. Configuring the Auto Scaling group to distribute instances across both AZs (using both subnets) ensures application redundancy. Configuring the **RDS DB instance for Multi-AZ deployment** ensures the database layer has an automatic synchronous replica in a different AZ, which handles failover seamlessly.
explanations.D: This option is technically incorrect because a single subnet cannot span multiple Availability Zones (AZs) in AWS. Subnets are strictly confined to one AZ. This configuration is not possible.
explanations.correct: To achieve high availability, both the application layer (EC2) and the data layer (RDS) must be resilient to an AZ failure. EC2 instances should be distributed across multiple AZs (using a dedicated subnet in each AZ) via an Auto Scaling Group. RDS must be configured for Multi-AZ deployment, which automatically provisions and manages a synchronous standby replica in a second AZ for automatic failover.

questions.text: A company collects data for temperature, humidity, and atmospheric pressure in cities across multiple continents. Each site generates about 500 GB of data daily and has a high-speed Internet connection. The company wants to aggregate the data from all global sites as quickly as possible into a single Amazon S3 bucket while minimizing operational complexity. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Turn on S3 Transfer Acceleration on the destination S3 bucket. Use multipart uploads to directly upload site data to the destination S3 bucket.
options.B: Upload the data from each site to an S3 bucket in the closest Region. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication to copy objects to the destination S3 bucket. Then remove the data from the origin S3 bucket.
options.C: Schedule AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device jobs daily to transfer data from each site to the closest Region. Use S3 Cross-Region Replication to copy objects to the destination S3 bucket.
options.D: Upload the data from each site to an Amazon EC2 instance in the closest Region. Store the data in an Amazon EBS volume. At regular intervals, take an EBS snapshot and copy it to the Region that contains the destination S3 bucket. Restore the EBS volume in that Region.

explanations.A: S3 Transfer Acceleration uses the globally distributed edge network to accelerate uploads into a central S3 bucket. With high-speed internet at each site and large daily upload sizes (500 GB per site), this is the fastest and least operationally complex approach. Multipart upload further improves transfer performance.
explanations.B: Cross-Region Replication requires storing data in intermediate regional buckets and managing cleanup. It increases latency, costs, and operational overhead compared to direct uploads via Transfer Acceleration.
explanations.C: Snowball Edge devices are intended for offline bulk transfers or limited-connectivity environments. Using daily Snowball jobs for 500 GB per site is highly operationally complex and unnecessary because the sites already have high-speed internet.
explanations.D: Sending data to EC2 instances, managing EBS volumes, taking snapshots, and copying them adds significant operational complexity and cost. It is much slower than uploading directly to S3 with acceleration.
explanations.correct: S3 Transfer Acceleration provides the fastest and simplest way to aggregate large volumes of data from distributed global sites into a single S3 bucket.

questions.text: A company is building an ecommerce web application on AWS. The application sends information about new orders to an Amazon API Gateway REST API to process. The company wants to ensure that orders are processed in the order that they are received. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use an API Gateway integration to publish a message to an Amazon SNS topic when the application receives an order. Subscribe an AWS Lambda function to the topic to perform processing.
options.B: Use an API Gateway integration to send a message to an Amazon SQS FIFO queue when the application receives an order. Configure the SQS FIFO queue to invoke an AWS Lambda function for processing.
options.C: Use an API Gateway authorizer to block any requests while the application processes an order.
options.D: Use an API Gateway integration to send a message to an Amazon SQS standard queue when the application receives an order. Configure the SQS standard queue to invoke an AWS Lambda function for processing.

explanations.A: SNS does not guarantee message ordering. With multiple subscribers or retries, order is not preserved, so it cannot meet strict first-in-first-out processing requirements.
explanations.B: SQS FIFO queues guarantee exact ordering and exactly-once processing. When API Gateway sends messages to an SQS FIFO queue, the system preserves the order in which orders arrive. Lambda can poll the FIFO queue and process orders sequentially.
explanations.C: An authorizer cannot enforce ordered processing. It only validates or rejects API requests based on authentication or custom logic.
explanations.D: SQS standard queues do not guarantee message ordering. They offer at-least-once delivery, which can lead to duplicates and out-of-order processing.
explanations.correct: SQS FIFO queues ensure that orders are processed in the exact order they are received, making option B the correct choice.

questions.text: A company currently stores 5 TB of data in on-premises block storage systems. The company's current storage solution provides limited space for additional data. The company runs applications on premises that must be able to retrieve frequently accessed data with low latency. The company requires a cloud-based storage solution. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

options.A: Use Amazon S3 File Gateway. Integrate S3 File Gateway with the on-premises applications to store and directly retrieve files by using the SMB file system.
options.B: Use an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway with cached volumes as iSCSI targets.
options.C: Use an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway with stored volumes as iSCSI targets.
options.D: Use an AWS Storage Gateway Tape Gateway. Integrate Tape Gateway with the on-premises applications to store virtual tapes in Amazon S3.

explanations.A: S3 File Gateway is designed for file-based workloads and exposes NFS/SMB shares. The company needs block storage, not file storage, and must integrate with existing block-storage applications.
explanations.B: Volume Gateway with cached volumes stores frequently accessed data locally and keeps the full dataset in Amazon S3. This provides low-latency access for hot data, unlimited cloud-backed scalability, and minimal on-premises storage needs. It is the most operationally efficient solution.
explanations.C: Stored volumes keep the full dataset on premises, with asynchronous backups to AWS. This does not solve the problem of limited local storage capacity.
explanations.D: Tape Gateway is used for backup and archival workflows. It is not suitable for low-latency application access or as primary block storage.
explanations.correct: Cached volumes provide local low-latency access while scaling storage in the cloud through Amazon S3, meeting performance and operational efficiency requirements.

questions.text: A company operates a food delivery service. The current architecture includes EC2 Auto Scaling groups for order collection and fulfillment. Order collection occurs quickly, but order fulfillment can take longer. Data must not be lost due to scaling events. How can the architecture scale adequately during peak hours?

options.A: Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the CPUUtilization metric for each instance in both Auto Scaling groups. Configure each Auto Scaling group's minimum capacity to meet its peak workload value.
options.B: Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the CPUUtilization metric for each instance in both Auto Scaling groups. Configure a CloudWatch alarm to invoke an Amazon SNS topic to create additional Auto Scaling groups on demand.
options.C: Provision two Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues. Use one SQS queue for order collection. Use the second SQS queue for order fulfillment. Configure the EC2 instances to poll their respective queues. Scale the Auto Scaling groups based on notifications that the queues send.
options.D: Provision two Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues. Use one SQS queue for order collection. Use the second SQS queue for order fulfillment. Configure the EC2 instances to poll their respective queues. Scale the Auto Scaling groups based on the number of messages in each queue.

explanations.A: Setting a fixed minimum capacity for peak workload can result in over-provisioning during off-peak hours and does not decouple the collection and fulfillment processes. It also does not prevent data loss during scaling.
explanations.B: Creating additional Auto Scaling groups via SNS is complex and introduces operational overhead. It is not a standard method for scaling based on workload demands and does not inherently decouple processes.
explanations.C: Scaling based on notifications from SQS may work, but SQS does not send push notifications to trigger scaling. EC2 instances must poll SQS to detect workload changes. This option is less precise and could lead to delays in scaling.
explanations.D: Using SQS queues for order collection and fulfillment decouples the processes. Auto Scaling groups can scale based on the number of messages in each queue, ensuring that EC2 instances scale dynamically with workload while preventing data loss. This approach provides reliability and operational efficiency.
explanations.correct: Decoupling with SQS and scaling based on queue length ensures both order collection and fulfillment scale appropriately while maintaining message durability.

questions.text: A company runs nightly batch jobs on EC2 instances from 12:00 AM to 06:00 AM. If a job fails, another instance reprocesses it. Which solution provides the instances MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Purchase a 1-year Savings Plan for Amazon EC2 that covers the instance family of the Auto Scaling group that the batch job uses.
options.B: Purchase a 1-year Reserved Instance for the specific instance type and operating system of the instances in the Auto Scaling group that the batch job uses.
options.C: Create a new launch template for the Auto Scaling group. Set the instances to Spot Instances. Set a policy to scale out based on CPU usage.
options.D: Create a new launch template for the Auto Scaling group. Increase the instance size. Set a policy to scale out based on CPU usage.

explanations.A: Savings Plans are better suited for continuous workloads (24/7). For a 6-hour daily batch, Spot instances offer much deeper discounts (up to 90%).
explanations.B: Reserved Instances require payment for the capacity regardless of whether it is used 6 hours or 24 hours a day. Spot is significantly cheaper for this duration.
explanations.C: Spot Instances are ideal for stateless, interruptible batch jobs. Since the application can reprocess failed jobs on another instance, the risk of Spot interruption is acceptable. This is the cheapest compute option.
explanations.D: Increasing instance size or staying on On-Demand is more expensive than using the Spot market.
explanations.correct: Spot instances provide the highest cost savings for workloads that are fault-tolerant and run for specific, non-continuous periods.

questions.text: A company has an Amazon S3 bucket that contains critical data. The company must protect the data from accidental deletion. Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Enable versioning on the S3 bucket.
options.B: Enable MFA Delete on the S3 bucket.
options.C: Create a bucket policy on the S3 bucket.
options.D: Enable default encryption on the S3 bucket.
options.E: Create a lifecycle policy for the objects in the S3 bucket.
