explanations.A: Versioning allows S3 to keep multiple variants of an object in the same bucket. When an object is deleted, S3 inserts a delete marker instead of removing the data permanently, allowing for easy restoration.
explanations.B: MFA Delete adds an extra layer of security by requiring multi-factor authentication for changing the versioning state of the bucket or permanently deleting an object version.
explanations.C: While a bucket policy can restrict who can delete objects, it does not provide a recovery mechanism for accidental deletions like versioning does.
explanations.D: Encryption protects data from unauthorized access or visibility but provides no protection against the deletion of the data itself.
explanations.E: Lifecycle policies are used to manage object retention and transition to other storage classes; if misconfigured, they can actually cause data to be deleted rather than protecting it.
explanations.correct: The combination of Versioning (for recovery) and MFA Delete (for prevention of permanent removal) is the AWS-recommended approach for accidental deletion protection.

questions.text: A company hosts its enterprise resource planning (ERP) system in the us-east-1 Region. The system runs on Amazon EC2 instances. Customers use a public API that is hosted on the EC2 instances to exchange information with the ERP system. International customers report slow API response times from their data centers. Which solution will improve response times for the international customers MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Create an AWS Direct Connect connection that has a public virtual interface (VIF) to provide connectivity from each customer's data center to us-east-1. Route customer API requests by using a Direct Connect gateway to the ERP system API.
options.B: Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the API. Configure the CachingOptimized managed cache policy to provide improved cache efficiency.
options.C: Set up AWS Global Accelerator. Configure listeners for the necessary ports. Configure endpoint groups for the appropriate Regions to distribute traffic. Create an endpoint in the group for the API.
options.D: Use AWS Site-to-Site VPN to establish dedicated VPN tunnels between Regions and customer networks. Route traffic to the API over the VPN connections.

explanations.A: Direct Connect provides dedicated connectivity but is expensive and requires setup at each customer site. It is not cost-effective for serving multiple international customers.
explanations.B: CloudFront improves performance for cacheable content. APIs that require dynamic requests/responses may not benefit fully from caching, limiting the effectiveness for improving latency for dynamic API traffic.
explanations.C: AWS Global Accelerator provides a fixed entry point with optimal routing over the AWS global network to reduce latency for international users. It is cost-effective and improves response times for dynamic API requests without requiring changes to the application.
explanations.D: Site-to-Site VPN adds complexity, requires setup at each customer location, and introduces variable latency. It is less cost-effective than using Global Accelerator.
explanations.correct: AWS Global Accelerator routes traffic over the AWS global network, reducing latency for international customers without complex networking setup, making it the most cost-effective solution.

questions.text: A company tracks customer satisfaction by using surveys on its website. Survey results must be processed automatically and be available for the previous 12 months. Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST scalable way?

options.A: Send the survey results data to an Amazon API Gateway endpoint that is connected to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Create an AWS Lambda function to poll the SQS queue, call Amazon Comprehend for sentiment analysis, and save the results to an Amazon DynamoDB table. Set the TTL for all records to 365 days in the future.
options.B: Send the survey results data to an API that is running on an Amazon EC2 instance. Configure the API to store the survey results as a new record in an Amazon DynamoDB table, call Amazon Comprehend for sentiment analysis, and save the results in a second DynamoDB table. Set the TTL for all records to 365 days in the future.
options.C: Write the survey results data to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use S3 Event Notifications to invoke an AWS Lambda function to read the data and call Amazon Rekognition for sentiment analysis. Store the sentiment analysis results in a second S3 bucket. Use S3 lifecycle policies on each bucket to expire objects after 365 days.
options.D: Send the survey results data to an Amazon API Gateway endpoint that is connected to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure the SQS queue to invoke an AWS Lambda function that calls Amazon Lex for sentiment analysis and saves the results to an Amazon DynamoDB table. Set the TTL for all records to 365 days in the future.

explanations.A: API Gateway + SQS + Lambda + Amazon Comprehend provides a fully serverless, event-driven architecture. SQS ensures decoupling and durability of survey results, Lambda provides automatic scaling, and DynamoDB with TTL retains data for 12 months. Using Comprehend provides accurate sentiment analysis. This solution scales efficiently during high traffic and requires minimal operational overhead.
explanations.B: Using an EC2 instance introduces operational overhead and is less scalable under high survey loads. Managing EC2 scaling and availability adds complexity compared to a serverless solution.
explanations.C: Amazon Rekognition is designed for image/video analysis, not text sentiment analysis. Using S3 + Lambda for storage is scalable, but sentiment analysis will not be correct using Rekognition.
explanations.D: Amazon Lex is intended for building conversational interfaces, not general sentiment analysis. Using Lex would not provide accurate sentiment analysis for survey text, making it unsuitable for this requirement.
explanations.correct: Option A uses fully serverless, scalable AWS services with correct sentiment analysis, durable storage, and automated retention for 12 months, meeting requirements efficiently.

questions.text: A company used an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance during application testing. Before terminating the DB instance, a solutions architect created a database dump using mysqldump and a final DB snapshot. The company now wants to create a MySQL-compatible edition of Amazon Aurora from these backups. Which solutions will create the new DB instance? (Choose two.)

options.A: Import the RDS snapshot directly into Aurora.
options.B: Upload the RDS snapshot to Amazon S3. Then import the RDS snapshot into Aurora.
options.C: Upload the database dump to Amazon S3. Then import the database dump into Aurora.
options.D: Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to import the RDS snapshot into Aurora.
options.E: Upload the database dump to Amazon S3. Then use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to import the database dump into Aurora.

explanations.A: Amazon Aurora allows you to migrate an existing Amazon RDS for MySQL DB snapshot directly into an Aurora MySQL DB cluster using the 'Migrate Database' feature in the console.
explanations.B: RDS snapshots are managed by the service and reside in the AWS infrastructure; there is no requirement or native path to manually 'upload' an RDS-managed snapshot to S3 before Aurora migration.
explanations.C: Aurora supports migrating data from MySQL by using mysqldump files. The standard procedure is to upload the dump file to an S3 bucket and then use the 'LOAD DATA FROM S3' or 'Restore from S3' functionality.
explanations.D: AWS DMS is used for live data migration between active endpoints. It does not natively 'import' a static RDS snapshot file as a source.
explanations.E: While DMS can use S3 as a source, it is more complex than the native Aurora import functionality for a single dump file and represents higher operational overhead in this scenario.
explanations.correct: Direct snapshot migration and S3-based dump imports are the two primary, native paths for moving RDS MySQL data to Aurora MySQL.

questions.text: A solutions architect is designing a VPC with public and private subnets in three Availability Zones. Private subnets require internet access for EC2 instances to download software updates. How should the architect enable internet access for the private subnets?

options.A: Create three NAT gateways, one for each public subnet in each AZ. Create a private route table for each AZ that forwards non-VPC traffic to the NAT gateway in its AZ.
options.B: Create three NAT instances, one for each private subnet in each AZ. Create a private route table for each AZ that forwards non-VPC traffic to the NAT instance in its AZ.
options.C: Create a second internet gateway on one of the private subnets. Update the route table for the private subnets that forward non-VPC traffic to the private internet gateway.
options.D: Create an egress-only internet gateway on one of the public subnets. Update the route table for the private subnets that forward non-VPC traffic to the egress-only Internet gateway.

explanations.A: Creating a NAT gateway in each AZ ensures high availability and allows instances in private subnets to access the internet for software updates. Each private route table routes non-VPC traffic to the NAT gateway in the same AZ, minimizing cross-AZ data transfer costs.
explanations.B: NAT instances require more management, do not scale automatically, and are less resilient than NAT gateways. They also introduce operational overhead.
explanations.C: You cannot attach a second internet gateway to a VPC; a VPC can have only one internet gateway. This option is invalid.
explanations.D: Egress-only internet gateways are used for IPv6 traffic only. The question specifies IPv4 CIDR blocks, so this solution is not applicable.
explanations.correct: NAT gateways in each AZ provide private subnets with internet access for IPv4 traffic, ensuring high availability and low operational overhead.

questions.text: A company operates a two-tier application for image processing in two Availability Zones. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) for the web tier uses public subnets, and EC2 instances for the application tier use private subnets. A security audit shows the application is receiving millions of illegitimate requests from a small number of IP addresses, causing performance issues. A solutions architect needs an immediate fix while a permanent solution is investigated. What should be recommended?

options.A: Modify the inbound security group for the web tier. Add a deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.
options.B: Modify the network ACL for the web tier subnets. Add an inbound deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.
options.C: Modify the inbound security group for the application tier. Add a deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.
options.D: Modify the network ACL for the application tier subnets. Add an inbound deny rule for the IP addresses that are consuming resources.

explanations.A: Security groups are stateful and support only 'allow' rules. It is impossible to add an explicit 'deny' rule to a security group.
explanations.B: Network ACLs (NACLs) are stateless and support both allow and deny rules. Adding a deny rule at the NACL level for the web tier subnets will block the illegitimate traffic before it reaches the ALB or the instances, alleviating the immediate performance load.
explanations.C: Security groups do not support deny rules. Additionally, the application tier is already protected by the web tier; blocking at the application tier still allows the web tier to be overwhelmed.
explanations.D: Blocking at the application tier subnets is too late in the request flow. Illegitimate requests would still hit the public-facing ALB and web tier, failing to resolve the immediate performance bottleneck.
explanations.correct: Network ACLs are the primary mechanism for blocking specific IP addresses or CIDR blocks at the subnet boundary in AWS.

questions.text: A global marketing company has applications running in the eu-west-1 Region that need to communicate securely with databases in the ap-southeast-2 Region. Which network design meets these requirements?

options.A: Create a VPC peering connection between the eu-west-1 VPC and the ap-southeast-2 VPC. Create an inbound rule in the eu-west-1 application security group that allows traffic from the database server IP addresses in the ap-southeast-2 security group.
options.B: Configure a VPC peering connection between the ap-southeast-2 VPC and the eu-west-1 VPC. Update the subnet route tables. Create an inbound rule in the ap-southeast-2 database security group that references the security group ID of the application servers in eu-west-1.
options.C: Configure a VPC peering connection between the ap-southeast-2 VPC and the eu-west-1 VPC. Update the subnet route tables. Create an inbound rule in the ap-southeast-2 database security group that allows traffic from the eu-west-1 application server IP addresses.
options.D: Create a transit gateway with a peering attachment between the eu-west-1 VPC and the ap-southeast-2 VPC. After the transit gateways are properly peered and routing is configured, create an inbound rule in the database security group that references the security group ID of the application servers in eu-west-1.

explanations.A: This option fails to mention updating route tables, which is required for peering. Furthermore, the inbound rule should be on the database security group to allow application traffic, not vice versa.
explanations.B: AWS does not support referencing security groups across Regions in a VPC peering connection. Security group referencing is only supported for intra-Region peering.
explanations.C: Cross-Region VPC peering requires manual route table updates in both VPCs. Since security group IDs cannot be referenced across Regions, the security group must be configured to allow traffic from the specific CIDR block or IP addresses of the peer VPC's application servers.
explanations.D: While Transit Gateway supports peering across Regions, it also does not support cross-Region security group referencing. This solution is also more operationally complex for a simple two-VPC connection.
explanations.correct: Security group rules for cross-Region peering must use CIDR blocks because security group ID referencing is limited to the same Region.

questions.text: A company's production environment runs EC2 On-Demand Instances constantly Monday–Saturday, and only 12 hours on Sunday. The Sunday instances cannot tolerate interruptions. The company wants to cost-optimize the environment. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Purchase Scheduled Reserved Instances for the EC2 instances that run for only 12 hours on Sunday. Purchase Standard Reserved Instances for the EC2 instances that run constantly between Monday and Saturday.
options.B: Purchase Convertible Reserved Instances for the EC2 instances that run for only 12 hours on Sunday. Purchase Standard Reserved Instances for the EC2 instances that run constantly between Monday and Saturday.
options.C: Use Spot Instances for the EC2 instances that run for only 12 hours on Sunday. Purchase Standard Reserved Instances for the EC2 instances that run constantly between Monday and Saturday.
options.D: Use Spot Instances for the EC2 instances that run for only 12 hours on Sunday. Purchase Convertible Reserved Instances for the EC2 instances that run constantly between Monday and Saturday.

explanations.A: Scheduled Reserved Instances allow cost savings for predictable workloads that run during specific times (like 12 hours on Sunday). Standard Reserved Instances provide cost savings for EC2 instances that run continuously Monday–Saturday. This combination optimizes costs while meeting the uptime requirement.
explanations.B: Convertible Reserved Instances allow instance type flexibility but do not provide scheduling benefits. They are less optimal for short, fixed-duration workloads like the 12-hour Sunday instances.
explanations.C: Spot Instances can be interrupted at any time and cannot guarantee uptime. Since the Sunday instances cannot tolerate interruptions, Spot Instances are not suitable.
explanations.D: Using Spot Instances for the Sunday workload is not suitable due to the no-interruption requirement, even though Standard or Convertible RIs could cover the other instances.

questions.text: A company's image-hosting website stores static content in an S3 bucket. Users around the world experience latency when uploading and downloading images. The company wants to improve website performance with the LEAST implementation effort. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the S3 bucket to improve the download performance. Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration to improve the upload performance.
options.B: Configure Amazon EC2 instances of the right sizes in multiple AWS Regions. Migrate the application to the EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute the website traffic equally among the EC2 instances. Configure AWS Global Accelerator to address global demand with low latency.
options.C: Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution that uses the S3 bucket as an origin to improve the download performance. Configure the application to use CloudFront to upload images to improve the upload performance. Create S3 buckets in multiple AWS Regions. Configure replication rules for the buckets to replicate users' data based on the users' location. Redirect downloads to the S3 bucket that is closest to each user's location.
options.D: Configure AWS Global Accelerator for the S3 bucket to improve network performance. Create an endpoint for the application to use Global Accelerator instead of the S3 bucket.

explanations.A: Using CloudFront as a CDN improves download performance globally, while S3 Transfer Acceleration optimizes uploads over long distances. This solution provides significant performance improvements with minimal changes to the existing architecture.
explanations.B: Migrating to EC2 instances in multiple Regions introduces significant operational complexity and overhead, which is unnecessary for a static S3-hosted website.
explanations.C: Creating multiple S3 buckets with replication and custom upload routing adds operational complexity and requires application changes, making it less efficient than using CloudFront and S3 Transfer Acceleration.
explanations.D: AWS Global Accelerator does not directly accelerate S3 uploads. CloudFront and S3 Transfer Acceleration are the recommended approaches for optimizing upload and download performance for S3-hosted websites.

questions.text: A company uses AWS Organizations and needs to ensure all infrastructure resources are backed up using AWS Backup. Resources are identified by tags, but some resources are currently untagged. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use AWS Config to identify all untagged resources. Tag the identified resources programmatically. Use tags in the backup plan.
options.B: Use AWS Config to identify all resources that are not running. Add those resources to the backup vault.
options.C: Require all AWS account owners to review their resources to identify the resources that need to be backed up.
options.D: Use Amazon Inspector to identify all noncompliant resources.

explanations.A: AWS Config can evaluate resources for the presence of specific tags. Remediation actions can be triggered to programmatically apply tags to non-compliant resources. AWS Backup plans then use these tags to automatically include resources in backup jobs, creating a fully automated workflow.
explanations.B: Resources that are not running might still need backups (e.g., EBS volumes, stopped EC2 instances). Furthermore, adding resources directly to a vault is not how backup scheduling is managed.
explanations.C: Manual review by account owners is time-consuming, prone to human error, and represents high operational overhead.
explanations.D: Amazon Inspector is used for security vulnerability scanning and network reachability analysis, not for resource inventory management or tagging compliance.
explanations.correct: Combining AWS Config for compliance monitoring and automated remediation with tag-based AWS Backup plans provides a highly efficient, scalable governance model.

questions.text: A company uses AWS Systems Manager for routine management and patching of Amazon EC2 instances in an IP address type target group behind an ALB. New security protocols require instances to be removed from service during patching. Errors occur when following the new protocol. Which combination of solutions will resolve the errors? (Choose two.)

options.A: Change the target type of the target group from IP address type to instance type.
options.B: Continue to use the existing Systems Manager document without changes because it is already optimized to handle instances that are in an IP address type target group behind an ALB.
options.C: Implement the AWSEC2-PatchLoadBalanacerInstance Systems Manager Automation document to manage the patching process.
options.D: Use Systems Manager Maintenance Windows to automatically remove the instances from service to patch the instances.
options.E: Configure Systems Manager State Manager to remove the instances from service and manage the patching schedule. Use ALB health checks to re-route traffic.

explanations.A: Changing the target type from IP to instance type is not necessary. Systems Manager can manage instances in IP target groups without changing target types.
explanations.B: The existing document is insufficient to handle the new requirement of safely removing instances from service during patching. Continuing without changes will not resolve the errors.
explanations.C: The AWSEC2-PatchLoadBalancerInstance Automation document is designed to safely remove EC2 instances from an ALB target group, perform patching, and then re-register them. This resolves patching errors related to ALB target group integration.
explanations.D: Systems Manager Maintenance Windows can automate the process of removing instances from service during patching. It ensures that instances are not serving traffic while patches are applied, preventing errors during the patch window.
explanations.E: State Manager alone does not automatically handle removal from ALB target groups for patching purposes, making it insufficient for this use case.
explanations.correct: Implementing AWSEC2-PatchLoadBalancerInstance and using Maintenance Windows ensures instances are safely removed from service during patching and re-registered after, resolving the errors.

questions.text: A company has an automobile sales website using Amazon RDS. When a car is sold, the listing must be removed and data sent to multiple target systems. Which design should a solutions architect recommend?

options.A: Create an AWS Lambda function triggered when the database on Amazon RDS is updated to send the information to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue for the targets to consume.
options.B: Create an AWS Lambda function triggered when the database on Amazon RDS is updated to send the information to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue for the targets to consume.
options.C: Subscribe to an RDS event notification and send an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue fanned out to multiple Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topics. Use AWS Lambda functions to update the targets.
options.D: Subscribe to an RDS event notification and send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic fanned out to multiple Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queues. Use AWS Lambda functions to update the targets.

explanations.A: Lambda triggered directly on RDS updates is not natively supported; using SQS alone does not provide a reliable fan-out mechanism to multiple targets.
explanations.B: Using SQS FIFO provides ordering but does not efficiently fan out messages to multiple targets.
explanations.C: Fan-out from SQS to SNS is not a supported architecture; SNS typically fans out to SQS or Lambda.
explanations.D: Subscribing to RDS events, sending them to an SNS topic, and then fanning out to multiple SQS queues is a scalable and reliable event-driven design. Lambda functions can then consume from SQS to update each target system independently.

questions.text: A company is developing an application to provide order shipping statistics via a REST API. The company wants to extract these statistics every morning, format them into an HTML report, and email the report to several recipients. Which combination of steps should be taken?

options.A: Configure the application to send the data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose.
options.B: Use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to format the data and to send the report by email.
options.C: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) scheduled event that invokes an AWS Glue job to query the application's API for the data.
options.D: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) scheduled event that invokes an AWS Lambda function to query the application's API for the data.
options.E: Store the application data in Amazon S3. Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic as an S3 event destination to send the report by email.

explanations.A: Kinesis Data Firehose is used for real-time streaming data ingestion and delivery, not for scheduled polling of a REST API.
explanations.B: Amazon SES is a professional email service that supports complex HTML formatting and attachments, making it the ideal choice for sending formatted reports.
explanations.C: AWS Glue is an ETL service designed for large-scale data processing and is over-engineered for querying a simple REST API and sending a report.
explanations.D: Amazon EventBridge can trigger a Lambda function on a cron schedule. The Lambda function can efficiently query the REST API, process the results, and trigger the email delivery.
explanations.E: Amazon SNS email notifications are primarily for plain-text alerts and do not support the rich HTML formatting required for a formal report.
explanations.correct: An EventBridge-triggered Lambda function provides the compute for scheduled API polling, and SES provides the necessary formatting and delivery capabilities for HTML reports.

questions.text:
A global company hosts its web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The web application has static data and dynamic data. The company stores its static data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The company wants to improve performance and reduce latency for the static data and dynamic data. The company is using its own domain name registered with Amazon Route 53.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that has the S3 bucket and the ALB as origins. Configure Route 53 to route traffic to the CloudFront distribution.
options.B: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that has the ALB as an origin. Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator that has the S3 bucket as an endpoint Configure Route 53 to route traffic to the CloudFront distribution.
options.C: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that has the S3 bucket as an origin. Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator that has the ALB and the CloudFront distribution as endpoints. Create a custom domain name that points to the accelerator DNS name. Use the custom domain name as an endpoint for the web application.
options.D: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution that has the ALB as an origin. Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator that has the S3 bucket as an endpoint. Create two domain names. Point one domain name to the CloudFront DNS name for dynamic content. Point the other domain name to the accelerator DNS name for static content. Use the domain names as endpoints for the web application.

explanations.A: **Amazon CloudFront is the key service for reducing latency for both static and dynamic content.** By using CloudFront with **multiple origins** (S3 for static data and the ALB for dynamic data), a single distribution can serve all content. CloudFront will cache static data at edge locations globally (reducing S3 latency) and use persistent connections and the AWS private backbone to accelerate dynamic content requests to the ALB (reducing ALB latency). Route 53 is then configured with an Alias record pointing to the CloudFront distribution, providing a single endpoint for the company's domain name.
explanations.B: This solution incorrectly uses AWS Global Accelerator for the S3 bucket. Global Accelerator is designed to accelerate TCP/UDP traffic and improve availability by directing traffic to optimal endpoints. It does **not** provide the caching and content delivery capabilities needed for static data; that is CloudFront's purpose. The combination is unnecessarily complex and less effective than using CloudFront for both.
explanations.C: This solution is overly complex. AWS Global Accelerator is not typically placed *in front* of a CloudFront distribution, as CloudFront already uses a global edge network. CloudFront's capabilities (caching for static and acceleration for dynamic) are sufficient for this requirement and are simpler to configure than introducing Global Accelerator.
explanations.D: While possible, using two separate domain names and two different global services (CloudFront and Global Accelerator) to serve the same website adds significant configuration complexity for both the application (to reference two different domains) and the DNS setup, which is not the most straightforward solution. CloudFront is perfectly capable of handling both content types through a single distribution and domain name.

questions.text: A company needs to configure multiple development environments and PostgreSQL databases for its developers. Each environment is used for only half of an 8-hour workday on average. Which solution is MOST cost-effective?

options.A: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL database.
options.B: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Single-AZ DB instances.
options.C: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon Aurora On-Demand PostgreSQL-Compatible database.
options.D: Configure each development environment with its own Amazon S3 bucket by using Amazon S3 Object Select.

explanations.A: Provisioned Aurora instances incur charges as long as they are running. Since the environments are idle for the majority of the day, this is not cost-effective.
explanations.B: RDS instances are charged for every hour they are provisioned. While Single-AZ is cheaper than Multi-AZ, it still requires manual or scripted stopping/starting to optimize costs for a 4-hour workday.
explanations.C: Amazon Aurora Serverless (referenced here as 'On-Demand') automatically scales capacity up and down and can pause during periods of inactivity. This ensures the company only pays for the database capacity consumed during the active 4 hours of use, making it the most cost-effective for intermittent development workloads.
explanations.D: S3 Object Select is a feature for querying data within S3 objects using SQL; it is not a relational database service and cannot replace a PostgreSQL database schema.
explanations.correct: Aurora Serverless is specifically designed for infrequent, intermittent, or unpredictable workloads, offering the best cost profile by charging only for active seconds of use.

questions.text: An application runs on Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zonas. The instances run in an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. The application performs best when the CPU utilization of the EC2 instances is at or near 40%. What should a solutions architect do to maintain the desired performance across all instances in the group?

options.A: Use a simple scaling policy to dynamically scale the Auto Scaling group.
options.B: Use a target tracking policy to dynamically scale the Auto Scaling group.
options.C: Use an AWS Lambda function ta update the desired Auto Scaling group capacity.
options.D: Use scheduled scaling actions to scale up and scale down the Auto Scaling group.

explanations.A: A simple scaling policy scales based on a single CloudWatch alarm, but it adjusts capacity by a fixed amount (e.g., 'add 2 instances'). It is not designed to maintain a specific utilization level like 40% efficiently. It can lead to 'fleeing the alarm' where the system oscillates.
explanations.B: A **target tracking scaling policy** is the ideal solution for this scenario. It allows the user to define a target value for a specific metric (in this case, 40% CPU Utilization). AWS Auto Scaling automatically adjusts the desired capacity of the Auto Scaling group to maintain that target utilization level, both scaling out (adding instances) and scaling in (removing instances) as load changes. This is the simplest and most effective way to maintain the desired performance.
explanations.C: Using an AWS Lambda function to update the desired capacity requires a custom solution to monitor metrics and calculate the capacity needed. This is high operational overhead and duplicates the functionality already provided by the managed Auto Scaling service.
explanations.D: Scheduled scaling actions are used to scale based on **predictable** load changes (e.g., 'every Monday at 9 AM'). This is not suitable for dynamic, real-time scaling based on an ongoing performance metric like CPU utilization.
explanations.correct: Target tracking scaling policies are specifically designed to automatically maintain a specified utilization level (like 40% CPU) by proactively managing the group's capacity in response to changing load, ensuring optimal performance.

questions.text: A company’s website provides users with downloadable historical performance reports. The website needs a solution that will scale to meet the company’s website demands globally. The solution should be cost-effective, limit the provisioning of infrastructure resources, and provide the fastest possible response time. Which combination should a solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements?

options.A: Amazon CloudFront and Amazon S3
options.B: AWS Lambda and Amazon DynamoDB
options.C: Application Load Balancer with Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling
options.D: Amazon Route 53 with internal Application Load Balancers

explanations.A: **Amazon S3** is a highly durable, scalable, and cost-effective object storage service, which is perfect for storing downloadable files like reports. **Amazon CloudFront** is a Content Delivery Network (CDN) that caches content at edge locations globally. This combination meets all requirements: it **scales globally** and provides the **fastest response time** (by serving content from the nearest edge location), is highly **cost-effective** (S3 is cheap, and CloudFront reduces expensive cross-Region data transfer), and **limits infrastructure provisioning** (both S3 and CloudFront are fully managed, serverless services).
explanations.B: AWS Lambda and Amazon DynamoDB are generally used for dynamic applications and storing structured data, not for serving large, static downloadable files. DynamoDB is not a cost-effective choice for bulk storage, and this serverless compute/database pair does not use a global CDN to achieve the 'fastest possible response time' for static content.
explanations.C: This solution uses provisioned EC2 instances, which requires infrastructure management (OS patching, capacity planning, security groups) and fails to meet the requirement to **limit the provisioning of infrastructure resources** and minimize operational overhead. It's also not optimized for global delivery/fastest response time compared to a CDN.
explanations.D: Route 53 with Application Load Balancers (ALBs) can route traffic globally, but it only routes to the nearest AWS Region, not to an edge cache close to the user, meaning it does not provide the **fastest possible response time** that a CDN like CloudFront can offer for downloadable files. It also still relies on provisioned infrastructure behind the ALB.
explanations.correct: The combination of Amazon S3 for cost-effective storage and Amazon CloudFront for high-performance, global caching is the standard and most optimal solution for serving static downloadable files with minimum infrastructure provisioning.

questions.text: A company is migrating a microservices application to an Amazon EKS cluster. The company must configure the Amazon EKS control plane with endpoint private access set to true and endpoint public access set to false for security compliance. The worker nodes are in private subnets. However, the nodes cannot join the cluster. Which solution will allow the nodes to join the cluster?

options.A: Grant the required permission in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to the AmazonEKSNodeRole IAM role.
options.B: Create interface VPC endpoints to allow nodes to access the control plane.
options.C: Recreate nodes in the public subnet. Restrict security groups for EC2 nodes.
options.D: Allow outbound traffic in the security group of the nodes.

explanations.A: While the AmazonEKSNodeRole is required for node operation, the error 'cannot join the cluster' in a private-only endpoint configuration typically points to a network connectivity issue to the EKS API server.
explanations.B: When public access to the EKS cluster endpoint is disabled, nodes must communicate with the control plane through the private endpoint. In a VPC without an internet gateway or NAT gateway, worker nodes require VPC interface endpoints (AWS PrivateLink) to communicate with the EKS API and other AWS services.
explanations.C: Moving nodes to a public subnet violates the security compliance requirement to keep the data plane in private subnets.
explanations.D: Allowing outbound traffic is insufficient if there is no route to the EKS control plane endpoint, which is isolated from the public internet in this configuration.
explanations.correct: Worker nodes in private subnets require interface VPC endpoints to reach the EKS API server (control plane) when public access is disabled, ensuring secure and private communication within the VPC.

questions.text:
A gaming company is designing a highly available architecture. The application runs on a modified Linux kernel and supports only UDP-based traffic. The company needs the front-end tier to provide the best possible user experience. That tier must have low latency, route traffic to the nearest edge location, and provide static IP addresses for entry into the application endpoints.
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Configure Amazon Route 53 to forward requests to an Application Load Balancer. Use AWS Lambda for the application in AWS Application Auto Scaling.
options.B: Configure Amazon CloudFront to forward requests to a Network Load Balancer. Use AWS Lambda for the application in an AWS Application Auto Scaling group.
options.C: Configure AWS Global Accelerator to forward requests to a Network Load Balancer. Use Amazon EC2 instances for the application in an EC2 Auto Scaling group.
options.D: Configure Amazon API Gateway to forward requests to an Application Load Balancer. Use Amazon EC2 instances for the application in an EC2 Auto Scaling group.

explanations.A: This option fails to meet several key requirements. Route 53 is a DNS service and offers latency-based routing but does not provide static IP addresses for the entry point. The Application Load Balancer (ALB) operates at Layer 7 (HTTP/HTTPS) and does not support the required UDP protocol. Lambda is generally used for serverless functions, not for hosting applications requiring a modified Linux kernel.
explanations.B: This option fails because CloudFront is primarily a Content Delivery Network (CDN) designed for caching and accelerating **HTTP/HTTPS** traffic (Layer 7). It does not natively support the required **UDP** protocol for the application's entry point. Furthermore, using Lambda for an application requiring a modified Linux kernel is unsuitable.
explanations.C: This option meets all requirements. **AWS Global Accelerator** provides static, Anycast IP addresses that route traffic to the nearest AWS edge location (which meets the low latency, nearest edge location, and static IP requirements). It operates at Layer 4 (TCP/UDP), which supports the application's **UDP-based traffic**. The **Network Load Balancer (NLB)** also operates at Layer 4 (supporting UDP) and can be used as an endpoint for Global Accelerator. **Amazon EC2 instances** are necessary to run an application that requires a **modified Linux kernel**, and an **EC2 Auto Scaling group** ensures high availability and scalability.
explanations.D: This option fails because **Amazon API Gateway** is designed for creating, publishing, maintaining, monitoring, and securing **REST, HTTP, and WebSocket APIs** (Layer 7). It does not support the required **UDP-based traffic**. The Application Load Balancer (ALB) also does not support UDP.
explanations.correct: AWS Global Accelerator is designed for performance improvement by using the AWS global network and edge locations. It provides static, public IP addresses and supports the required UDP protocol, routing traffic to the optimal AWS Region based on geography. The Network Load Balancer (NLB) supports UDP traffic and acts as the target for Global Accelerator. EC2 instances are required to host the custom application with a modified kernel, and an Auto Scaling group ensures high availability.

questions.text: A company wants to migrate its existing on-premises monolithic application to AWS. The company wants to keep as much of the front-end code and the backend code as possible. However, the company wants to break the application into smaller applications. A different team will manage each application. The company needs a highly scalable solution that minimizes operational overhead.

options.A: Host the application on AWS Lambda. Integrate the application with Amazon API Gateway.
options.B: Host the application with AWS Amplify. Connect the application to an Amazon API Gateway API that is integrated with AWS Lambda.
options.C: Host the application on Amazon EC2 instances. Set up an Application Load Balancer with EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group as targets.
options.D: Host the application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). Set up an Application Load Balancer with Amazon ECS as the target.

explanations.A: While AWS Lambda and API Gateway minimize operational overhead (serverless), Lambda is ideal for smaller, event-driven functions. Migrating a monolithic application and then breaking it into smaller parts, while **keeping as much of the backend code as possible**, is often challenging with the Lambda programming model and resource limits. Containers (ECS or EKS) are typically the best fit for 're-platforming' a monolith into smaller services with minimal code changes.
explanations.B: AWS Amplify is great for hosting front-end applications, and Lambda/API Gateway provides a serverless backend. However, similar to option A, this approach doesn't align well with the requirement to 'keep as much of the backend code as possible' from the original monolithic application. Containers are the better choice for re-platforming existing code.
explanations.C: Hosting on EC2 instances with an Auto Scaling group is highly scalable and available. However, it requires the company to manage the underlying operating system, patching, and scaling of the instances themselves (managing the servers). This results in a higher **operational overhead** than container or serverless solutions, failing to meet the requirement for minimal overhead.
explanations.D: **Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS)** with the **Fargate** launch type (for minimal operational overhead) is the ideal solution. Containers allow the company to easily break the monolithic application into smaller services (microservices) while **keeping the majority of the existing code structure** (retaining the modified kernel isn't mentioned here, but containerizing existing code is straightforward). ECS is highly scalable, and using Fargate minimizes operational overhead by eliminating the need to manage the EC2 instances, making it a better fit than EC2.
explanations.correct: Containerization (ECS/EKS) is the recommended approach for re-platforming monolithic applications into smaller, microservice-like applications while keeping most of the existing code. **Amazon ECS** minimizes operational overhead, especially when using the Fargate launch type, as AWS manages the underlying server infrastructure. It is highly scalable and available, aligning with all business requirements.

questions.text:
A large media company hosts a web application on AWS. The company wants to start caching confidential media files so that users around the world will have reliable access to the files. The content is stored in Amazon S3 buckets. The company must deliver the content quickly, regardless of where the requests originate geographically.
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Use AWS DataSync to connect the S3 buckets to the web application.
options.B: Deploy AWS Global Accelerator to connect the S3 buckets to the web application.
options.C: Deploy Amazon CloudFront to connect the S3 buckets to CloudFront edge servers.
options.D: Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to connect the S3 buckets to the web application.

explanations.A: AWS DataSync is a data transfer service used for migrating or replicating large amounts of data between on-premises storage systems and AWS Storage services (like S3). It is not a content delivery network (CDN) and does not provide caching or global low-latency delivery to end-users.
explanations.B: AWS Global Accelerator uses the AWS global network to route traffic to your application endpoints, improving availability and performance. While it improves performance, it focuses on routing traffic to origin resources (like EC2, ALB, or an S3 bucket *configured as a website endpoint*). It does not provide the primary functions of **caching** content at the edge locations, which is essential for delivering media files quickly worldwide and reducing load on the origin.
explanations.C: Amazon CloudFront is a Content Delivery Network (CDN). It caches content at **Edge Locations** geographically close to users worldwide. This fulfills the requirements for **caching** confidential media files, **delivering content quickly**, and ensuring reliable access **regardless of where the requests originate geographically**.
explanations.D: Amazon Simple Queue Service (SQS) is a fully managed message queuing service. It is used to decouple and scale microservices, distributed systems, and serverless applications. It has no function related to content caching or global content delivery.
explanations.correct: Amazon CloudFront is AWS's global Content Delivery Network (CDN) service. It uses a network of Edge Locations to cache content (including files from an S3 bucket) close to end-users worldwide, ensuring low-latency delivery and meeting the requirement for quick, global, and reliable access.

questions.text:
A company produces batch data that comes from different databases. The company also produces live stream data from network sensors and application APIs. The company needs to consolidate all the data into one place for business analytics. The company needs to process the incoming data and then stage the data in different Amazon S3 buckets. Teams will later run one-time queries and import the data into a business intelligence tool to show key performance indicators (KPIs).
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)

options.A: Use Amazon Athena for one-time queries. Use Amazon QuickSight to create dashboards for KPIs.
options.B: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics for one-time queries. Use Amazon QuickSight to create dashboards for KPIs.
options.C: Create custom AWS Lambda functions to move the individual records from the databases to an Amazon Redshift cluster.
options.D: Use an AWS Glue extract, transform, and load (ETL) job to convert the data into JSON format. Load the data into multiple Amazon OpenSearch Service (Amazon Elasticsearch Service) clusters.
options.E: Use blueprints in AWS Lake Formation to identify the data that can be ingested into a data lake. Use AWS Glue to crawl the source, extract the data, and load the data into Amazon S3 in Apache Parquet format.

explanations.A: This option provides the serverless data consumption and visualization layer. Athena is a serverless query engine perfect for ad-hoc/one-time queries on S3 (Data Lake) data, and QuickSight is a serverless BI service for KPIs, both minimizing operational overhead.
explanations.B: Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics is used for continuous, real-time analytics on streaming data, not primarily for running 'one-time queries' on data staged in S3, making it less suitable for the stated consumption pattern on the staged data.
explanations.C: Moving data to Amazon Redshift (a data warehouse) is an unnecessary step as the requirement is to stage data in S3. Furthermore, creating 'custom AWS Lambda functions' for ETL across various sources dramatically increases operational overhead, which the question seeks to minimize.
explanations.D: Loading the data into Amazon OpenSearch Service clusters adds operational overhead as clusters need to be managed. More importantly, it fails to meet the requirement to 'stage the data in different Amazon S3 buckets' for a pure Data Lake architecture, which is the clear pattern here.
explanations.E: This option provides the data ingestion, processing, and staging layer (Data Lake foundation). AWS Lake Formation blueprints and AWS Glue are managed, serverless services designed to automate the process of building, cleaning, and cataloging data into a Data Lake (S3), which minimizes operational overhead. Using Apache Parquet format is a best practice for high-performance, cost-optimized querying with services like Athena.
explanations.correct: The overall solution requires building a Data Lake on S3 with minimal overhead (E), and then providing serverless, efficient tools to analyze that data (A). Option E uses AWS Lake Formation and Glue to automate ingestion and format data into efficient Parquet in S3 (low overhead). Option A uses Amazon Athena for serverless queries on the S3 data and Amazon QuickSight for serverless business intelligence and KPIs.

questions.text:
A solutions architect is optimizing a website for an upcoming musical event. Videos of the performances will be streamed in real time and then will be available on demand. The event is expected to attract a global online audience.
Which service will improve the performance of both the real-time and on-demand streaming?

options.A: Amazon CloudFront
options.B: AWS Global Accelerator
options.C: Amazon Route 53
options.D: Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration

explanations.A: Amazon CloudFront is a Content Delivery Network (CDN) that uses a global network of Edge Locations to cache and deliver content closer to the user. CloudFront is specifically designed and optimized for both **Video-on-Demand (VOD)** (by caching the video segments) and **Live Streaming** (by rapidly delivering live manifests and segments) to a global audience with low latency.
explanations.B: AWS Global Accelerator is a networking service that routes user traffic over the highly optimized AWS global network to the nearest healthy application endpoint, improving performance for non-cacheable (dynamic) content or non-HTTP protocols. While it can improve the performance of the live stream connection, it does not provide the **caching** functionality essential for efficient, scalable **on-demand** content delivery, nor is it the primary solution for all-encompassing media delivery.
explanations.C: Amazon Route 53 is a highly available and scalable cloud Domain Name System (DNS) web service. It translates domain names to IP addresses and can perform traffic routing, but it does not directly speed up content delivery or provide edge caching for video segments.
explanations.D: Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration accelerates the transfer of files *into* an S3 bucket from a far-away client. It is used for ingestion/uploading of data, not for high-performance delivery/streaming of content *out* to a global audience.
explanations.correct: Amazon CloudFront is the only option that is a global Content Delivery Network (CDN) optimized for both Live Streaming (real-time) and Video-on-Demand (on-demand). It improves performance by caching content and delivering it through its network of Edge Locations, ensuring low latency for users worldwide.

questions.text: A company wants to send all AWS Systems Manager Session Manager logs to an Amazon S3 bucket for archival purposes. Which solution will meet this requirement with the MOST operational efficiency?

options.A: Enable S3 logging in the Systems Manager console. Choose an S3 bucket to send the session data to.
options.B: Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent. Push all logs to a CloudWatch log group. Export the logs to an S3 bucket from the group for archival purposes.
options.C: Create a Systems Manager document to upload all server logs to a central S3 bucket. Use Amazon EventBridge to run the Systems Manager document against all servers that are in the account daily.
options.D: Install an Amazon CloudWatch agent. Push all logs to a CloudWatch log group. Create a CloudWatch logs subscription that pushes any incoming log events to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Set Amazon S3 as the destination.

explanations.A: Systems Manager Session Manager has a native, built-in feature to send session logs directly to an S3 bucket. Enabling this in the console or via the API is the most direct and operationally efficient method as it requires no agents or intermediate services.
explanations.B: This approach introduces high operational overhead by requiring agent installation and manual/scheduled export tasks from CloudWatch to S3.
explanations.C: Using a custom document and EventBridge to run daily is inefficient compared to the real-time, native logging capability of Session Manager.
explanations.D: While this creates a streaming pipeline, it is far more complex and costly to manage than simply enabling the native S3 logging feature in Systems Manager.
explanations.correct: Leveraging the native integration between Session Manager and S3 provides an automated, serverless, and agentless solution for log archival.

questions.text: Organizers for a global event want to put daily reports online as static HTML pages. The pages are expected to generate millions of views from users around the world. The files are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. A solutions architect has been asked to design an efficient and effective solution. Which action should the solutions architect take to accomplish this?

options.A: Generate presigned URLs for the files.
options.B: Use cross-Region replication to all Regions.
options.C: Use the geoproximity feature of Amazon Route 53.
options.D: Use Amazon CloudFront with the S3 bucket as its origin.

explanations.A: Presigned URLs are used for granting temporary, limited access to private S3 objects. They do not address the requirements for global scale, high efficiency, and performance for millions of views.
explanations.B: Cross-Region replication improves availability and can reduce latency by moving data closer to users, but it still requires users to access the data directly from an S3 bucket in a specific region, which is not as efficient as a global CDN for high-volume reads.
explanations.C: Geoproximity routing with Route 53 is a useful traffic management feature, but it directs traffic to a regional endpoint (like an S3 bucket or EC2 instance). It doesn't provide the high performance, caching, and global edge network benefits of a Content Delivery Network (CDN) for serving static content.
explanations.D: Amazon CloudFront is a global Content Delivery Network (CDN) service that caches content at edge locations worldwide. Using an S3 bucket as the origin and distributing content via CloudFront is the standard, most effective, and most efficient method to handle millions of views globally for static files, ensuring low latency and high performance.
explanations.correct: For serving static content with high performance and efficiency to a global audience with expected millions of views, Amazon CloudFront is the best solution as it leverages a global network of edge locations for caching and faster delivery.

questions.text: A social media company wants to allow users to upload images and automatically resize them for multiple device types. The application experiences unpredictable traffic. Which highly available solution maximizes scalability?

options.A: Create a static website hosted in Amazon S3 that invokes AWS Lambda functions to resize the images and store the images in an Amazon S3 bucket.
options.B: Create a static website hosted in Amazon CloudFront that invokes AWS Step Functions to resize the images and store the images in an Amazon RDS database.
options.C: Create a dynamic website hosted on a web server that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. Configure a process that runs on the EC2 instance to resize the images and store the images in an Amazon S3 bucket.
options.D: Create a dynamic website hosted on an automatically scaling Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that creates a resize job in Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS). Set up an image-resizing program that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance to process the resize jobs.

explanations.A: Using S3 for static hosting and Lambda for event-driven image processing provides a serverless, highly available architecture that scales automatically and instantly to handle unpredictable traffic with zero server management.
explanations.B: Amazon RDS is for relational data and is not an appropriate or scalable choice for storing binary image files. Step Functions are used for orchestration, not direct image processing.
explanations.C: A single EC2 instance is a single point of failure and does not scale well to handle unpredictable traffic bursts without complex management.
explanations.D: While ECS and SQS are scalable, this solution introduces significantly more operational overhead (managing clusters, SQS consumers, and EC2 instances) compared to the serverless S3/Lambda approach.
explanations.correct: The combination of S3 and Lambda offers a 'well-architected' serverless pattern for image processing that prioritizes scalability and high availability.

questions.text: A gaming company hosts a browser-based application on AWS. The users of the application consume a large number of videos and images that are stored in Amazon S3. This content is the same for all users. The application has increased in popularity, and millions of users worldwide accessing these media files. The company wants to provide the files to the users while reducing the load on the origin. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Deploy an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator in front of the web servers.
options.B: Deploy an Amazon CloudFront web distribution in front of the S3 bucket.
options.C: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis instance in front of the web servers.
options.D: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached instance in front of the web servers.

explanations.A: AWS Global Accelerator uses the AWS global network to improve performance by routing user traffic to the closest edge location, but it primarily targets non-cached applications and does not have the robust caching capabilities of a Content Delivery Network (CDN) necessary to handle millions of worldwide media requests and reduce origin load cost-effectively.
explanations.B: Amazon CloudFront is a global Content Delivery Network (CDN) specifically designed to cache static content (like videos and images) at edge locations worldwide. Placing it in front of the S3 bucket means the vast majority of requests are served from the cache, reducing latency, improving performance for worldwide users, and significantly lowering the load and cost on the S3 origin. This is the standard, most effective, and most cost-effective solution for serving popular static files globally.
explanations.C: Amazon ElastiCache (Redis) is an in-memory caching service used primarily to accelerate dynamic web applications by caching database queries or session data. It is a regional service and is not designed to distribute and cache static media files globally to millions of users, nor would it significantly reduce the load on the S3 origin.
explanations.D: Amazon ElastiCache (Memcached), similar to Redis, is a regional in-memory caching service for dynamic data. It is inappropriate for globally distributing static media files like videos and images from S3.
explanations.correct: Amazon CloudFront is the best solution for globally distributing high-volume static content from an S3 origin. Its global network and caching significantly improve performance, reduce latency for worldwide users, and minimize the load and retrieval costs from the origin bucket.

questions.text:
An entertainment company is using Amazon DynamoDB to store media metadata. The application is read intensive and experiencing delays. The company does not have staff to handle additional operational overhead and needs to improve the performance efficiency of DynamoDB without reconfiguring the application.
What should a solutions architect recommend to meet this requirement?

options.A: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.
options.B: Use Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX).
options.C: Replicate data by using DynamoDB global tables.
options.D: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached with Auto Discovery enabled.

explanations.A: Amazon ElastiCache for Redis is a highly effective caching solution, but integrating it requires the application to be modified to check the cache before querying DynamoDB (cache-aside logic). The requirement is to improve performance **without reconfiguring the application**.
explanations.B: Amazon DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is a fully managed, highly available in-memory cache for DynamoDB. It is designed to be API-compatible with DynamoDB, meaning it requires minimal (often zero) code changes to the application. The application simply changes the endpoint from the DynamoDB service endpoint to the DAX cluster endpoint. This meets the requirement for improved performance with no operational overhead and no application reconfiguration.
explanations.C: DynamoDB global tables are used for multi-Region, active-active redundancy to provide low-latency reads for globally distributed users. While it is a fully managed service, its primary function is not simply local read performance enhancement but multi-region replication. Using a global table in a single region does not provide the same performance boost as a dedicated in-memory cache and does not inherently meet the 'without reconfiguring the application' requirement as directly as DAX.
explanations.D: Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached also requires code changes to implement cache-aside logic, similar to ElastiCache for Redis. This violates the 'without reconfiguring the application' constraint.
explanations.correct: DAX is the specific AWS service created to address high-read-volume performance issues for DynamoDB with the key benefit of requiring minimal to zero application code changes, as the DAX client manages the caching logic internally and is API-compatible.

questions.text: A company is migrating an on-premises application to AWS and wants to use Amazon Redshift. Which use cases are suitable for Amazon Redshift in this scenario? (Choose three.)

options.A: Supporting data APIs to access data with traditional, containerized, and event-driven applications
options.B: Supporting client-side and server-side encryption
options.C: Building analytics workloads during specified hours and when the application is not active
options.D: Caching data to reduce the pressure on the backend database
options.E: Scaling globally to support petabytes of data and tens of millions of requests per minute
options.F: Creating a secondary replica of the cluster by using the AWS Management Console

explanations.A: The Amazon Redshift Data API allows applications (including serverless and containerized) to interact with Redshift without managing persistent connections, enabling modern application integration.
explanations.B: While Redshift supports encryption, encryption is a security feature/capability rather than a specific architectural 'use case' for choosing a data warehouse over other options.
explanations.C: Redshift is ideal for complex OLAP (Online Analytical Processing) workloads, and features like scheduled queries allow for batch analytics during off-peak times.
explanations.D: Redshift is an OLAP data warehouse, not a caching layer. Amazon ElastiCache is the correct service for reducing database pressure via caching.
explanations.E: Amazon Redshift is built for petabyte-scale data warehousing. With features like Concurrency Scaling, it can support massive growth in users and requests while maintaining performance.
explanations.F: Amazon Redshift clusters are not replicated via a simple 'secondary replica' toggle in the console in the same way as RDS; high availability is achieved within the cluster (RA3 nodes/Managed Storage) or via cross-region snapshots.
explanations.correct: Redshift's primary value lies in its massive scalability for analytical workloads and its modern Data API for cross-service integration.

questions.text: A company has an ordering application that stores customer information in Amazon RDS for MySQL. During regular business hours, employees run one-time queries for reporting purposes. Timeouts are occurring during order processing because the reporting queries are taking a long time to run. The company needs to eliminate the timeouts without preventing employees from performing queries. What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.A: Create a read replica. Move reporting queries to the read replica.
options.B: Create a read replica. Distribute the ordering application to the primary DB instance and the read replica.
options.C: Migrate the ordering application to Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity.
options.D: Schedule the reporting queries for non-peak hours.

explanations.A: Amazon RDS Read Replicas are designed to offload read-heavy workloads, such as reporting and analytical queries, from the primary database instance . By directing the long-running reporting queries to the Read Replica, the primary DB instance is freed up to handle the transactional ordering application workload (writes and short reads) without timeouts. This meets all requirements: eliminating timeouts, allowing queries during business hours, and doing so with a fully managed solution.
explanations.B: The primary DB instance handles all write operations and is the authoritative source. The ordering application must write data, so it must primarily target the master DB instance. Distributing the entire transactional ordering application across both the primary and the read replica means that the application would attempt to write to the read replica (which is not allowed) or would need complex, error-prone logic to distinguish between read and write requests, which is not the standard use case for read replicas.
explanations.C: Migrating the entire application to Amazon DynamoDB would be a major re-architecture effort, requiring significant operational overhead and code changes. While it can scale, it is an extreme solution that goes far beyond the request to address performance contention caused by reporting queries.
explanations.D: Scheduling the reporting queries for non-peak hours (nighttime) would prevent employees from performing queries during regular business hours, directly violating the requirement: 'without preventing employees from performing queries.'
explanations.correct: Creating a Read Replica and dedicating it to the read-intensive reporting queries is the standard and most efficient architectural pattern in RDS to separate the operational transaction workload (OLTP) from the analytical reporting workload (OLAP), thus ensuring both can operate simultaneously without interference.
explanations.references:
https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Overview.Replicas.html

AWS Well-Architected Framework: Performance Efficiency Pillar - Read/Write Splitting

questions.text: A hospital wants to create digital copies for its large collection of historical written records. The hospital will continue to add hundreds of new documents each day. The hospital’s data team will scan the documents and will upload the documents to the AWS Cloud. A solutions architect must implement a solution to analyze the documents, extract the medical information, and store the documents so that an application can run SQL queries on the data. The solution must maximize scalability and operational efficiency. Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Write the document information to an Amazon EC2 instance that runs a MySQL database.
options.B: Write the document information to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use Amazon Athena to query the data.
options.C: Create an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances to run a custom application that processes the scanned files and extracts the medical information.
options.D: Create an AWS Lambda function that runs when new documents are uploaded. Use Amazon Rekognition to convert the documents to raw text. Use Amazon Transcribe Medical to detect and extract relevant medical information from the text.
options.E: Create an AWS Lambda function that runs when new documents are uploaded. Use Amazon Textract to convert the documents to raw text. Use Amazon Comprehend Medical to detect and extract relevant medical information from the text.

explanations.A: Using a transactional MySQL database running on an EC2 instance is not ideal for storing unstructured, constantly growing analytical data that is meant to be queried in bulk. RDS or EC2 databases require manual scaling and maintenance, which increases operational overhead and limits scalability compared to a data lake solution.
explanations.B: Storing the extracted data in Amazon S3 is the foundation of a highly scalable and cost-effective data lake . **Amazon Athena** is a serverless interactive query service that allows running standard SQL queries directly against data stored in S3, eliminating the need to load data into a traditional database. This maximizes scalability and minimizes operational efficiency. This satisfies the storage and SQL query requirement.
explanations.C: Using an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances for document processing and extraction requires the user to manage the operating system, runtime, patching, and the custom application code. This significantly increases **operational overhead** compared to using specialized, fully managed AI services and serverless compute like Lambda.
explanations.D: This option uses the wrong AWS AI services. **Amazon Rekognition** is primarily for image and video analysis (e.g., detecting objects, faces, or text in photos/videos), while **Amazon Textract** is the correct service for Optical Character Recognition (OCR) and structured data extraction from documents and scanned forms. **Amazon Transcribe Medical** is for converting **speech-to-text** (audio), not for analyzing extracted medical text. Therefore, this combination fails to meet the core functional requirements.
explanations.E: This is the ideal combination for the processing workflow. The workflow is triggered by an event (S3 upload) using the serverless **AWS Lambda** . **Amazon Textract** is the correct service for OCR and extracting text from scanned documents. **Amazon Comprehend Medical** is the correct service for Natural Language Processing (NLP) to detect and extract relevant medical entities, dosages, and conditions from the raw text. This serverless, event-driven approach maximizes scalability and operational efficiency. This satisfies the analysis and extraction requirement.
explanations.correct: The most operationally efficient and scalable solution uses serverless, specialized AI services for processing and a serverless data lake architecture for storage and querying. Amazon Textract and Comprehend Medical handle document processing and medical data extraction, while S3 and Athena provide a scalable, SQL-queryable data lake.
explanations.references:
https://aws.amazon.com/textract/

https://aws.amazon.com/comprehend/medical/

https://aws.amazon.com/athena/

AWS Serverless Image and Document Processing Patterns

questions.text: A company is running a batch application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application consists of a backend with multiple Amazon RDS databases. The application is causing a high number of reads on the databases. A solutions architect must reduce the number of database reads while ensuring high availability. What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement?

options.A: Add Amazon RDS read replicas.
options.B: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis.
options.C: Use Amazon Route 53 DNS caching
options.D: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached.

explanations.A: Adding Amazon RDS Read Replicas offloads read traffic from the primary database, which reduces the load on the master instance. However, the total number of database reads across the RDS cluster (primary + replicas) remains the same. Read replicas help with **read scaling**, but not with reducing the **number** of overall reads against the database layer, which is the core problem. Furthermore, for high availability, the replication might be eventually consistent.
explanations.B: **Amazon ElastiCache for Redis** is an in-memory data store service that is purpose-built for caching frequently accessed data . Placing a cache layer in front of the database significantly reduces the number of reads that hit the RDS instance, as subsequent requests for the same data are served from the much faster cache. Redis clusters offer multi-AZ replication, ensuring high availability and meeting all requirements. This is the optimal solution for reducing database read load.
explanations.C: Amazon Route 53 DNS caching controls how long a DNS record is cached by client resolvers (TTL). This affects name resolution speed but has no effect whatsoever on the frequency or volume of database reads performed by the application, making it irrelevant to the problem.
explanations.D: Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached is also a valid caching solution that reduces database reads. However, in the context of high availability, **Redis** is generally preferred because it natively supports data persistence and more robust high availability features like multi-AZ replication and automatic failover, whereas Memcached is simpler and does not offer native persistence or replication features, making Redis the more complete solution to ensure high availability.
explanations.correct: Implementing an in-memory caching layer using Amazon ElastiCache for Redis is the most effective way to reduce the number of reads hitting the database. Redis is highly scalable and provides built-in replication and partitioning for high availability.
explanations.references:
https://aws.amazon.com/elasticache/redis/

AWS Well-Architected Framework: Performance Efficiency Pillar - Caching Strategies

questions.text: A company provides a financial information API and expects peak usage times. The API must respond with consistently low latency. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use an Application Load Balancer and Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS).
options.B: Use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda functions with provisioned concurrency.
options.C: Use an Application Load Balancer and an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster.
options.D: Use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda functions with reserved concurrency.

explanations.A: ECS requires managing container definitions, clusters, and task scaling, which represents more operational overhead than a serverless API Gateway/Lambda approach.
explanations.B: Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda are serverless, minimizing overhead. Provisioned Concurrency pre-warms Lambda execution environments, eliminating cold starts and ensuring consistently low latency during peak traffic.
explanations.C: Amazon EKS has the highest operational overhead among the options, requiring Kubernetes management and cluster scaling.
explanations.D: Reserved Concurrency limits the maximum number of concurrent executions to protect other functions or downstream resources; it does not eliminate cold starts or ensure low latency for bursty traffic.
explanations.correct: Provisioned Concurrency is specifically designed to provide low, consistent latency for serverless APIs by managing execution environment initialization.

questions.text: An ecommerce company wants to launch a one-deal-a-day website on AWS. Each day will feature exactly one product on sale for a period of 24 hours. The company wants to be able to handle millions of requests each hour with millisecond latency during peak hours. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use Amazon S3 to host the full website in different S3 buckets. Add Amazon CloudFront distributions. Set the S3 buckets as origins for the distributions. Store the order data in Amazon S3.
options.B: Deploy the full website on Amazon EC2 instances that run in Auto Scaling groups across multiple Availability Zones. Add an Application Load Balancer (ALB) to distribute the website traffic. Add another ALB for the backend APIs. Store the data in Amazon RDS for MySQL.
options.C: Migrate the full application to run in containers. Host the containers on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Use the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler to increase and decrease the number of pods to process bursts in traffic. Store the data in Amazon RDS for MySQL.
options.D: Use an Amazon S3 bucket to host the website's static content. Deploy an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Set the S3 bucket as the origin. Use Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda functions for the backend APIs. Store the data in Amazon DynamoDB.

explanations.A: Hosting the full website in S3 and caching via CloudFront is excellent for static content (low latency and high scale). However, attempting to store transactional order data directly in S3 for real-time processing and retrieval is inefficient and unsuitable for transactional e-commerce workloads, which require structured, immediate updates/retrievals.
