questions.text: A company created a new organization in AWS Organizations. The organization has multiple accounts for thecompany's development teams. The development team members use AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to access the accounts. For each of the company's applications, the development teams must use a predefinedapplication name to tag resources that are created. A solutions architect needs to design a solution that gives the development team the ability to create resources only if the application name tag has an approved value. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Create an IAM group that has a conditional Allow policy that requires the application name tag to be specifiedfor resources to be created.
options.B: Create a cross-account role that has a Deny policy for any resource that has the application name tag.
options.C: Create a resource group in AWS Resource Groups to validate that the tags are applied to all resources in allaccounts.
options.D: Create a tag policy in Organizations that has a list of allowed application names.

explanations.correct:
IAM is AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) is the central service for controlling access to AWS resources. It helps you centrally manage permissions and strict authentication for users and workloads.

To address the requirements in this scenario, utilizing IAM is the optimal choice. This solution is designed for managing granular access policies, roles, and user identities across AWS. This aligns with the goal of Security and ensures the architecture is robust and follows AWS best practices.

Hence, the correct answer is: Create a tag policy in Organizations that has a list of allowed application names.
explanations.A: The option that says: 'Create an IAM group that has a conditional Allow policy that requires the application name tag to be specifiedfor resources to be created.' is incorrect. While this option mentions IAM, the specific configuration is not ideal. IAM is for permission management, not for network-level security or data encryption itself. The proposed method may introduce operational overhead or fail to meet the specific requirements of the scenario.
explanations.B: The option that says: 'Create a cross-account role that has a Deny policy for any resource that has the application name tag.' is incorrect. This approach represents a generic or custom solution that lacks the managed benefits of a dedicated AWS service. It typically adds complexity and maintenance effort compared to using the native features of the correct service.
explanations.C: The option that says: 'Create a resource group in AWS Resource Groups to validate that the tags are applied to all resources in allaccounts.' is incorrect. This approach represents a generic or custom solution that lacks the managed benefits of a dedicated AWS service. It typically adds complexity and maintenance effort compared to using the native features of the correct service.

questions.text: A company uses Amazon EC2 instances and stores data on Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes.The company must ensure that all data is encrypted at rest by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).The company must be able to control rotation of the encryption keys. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Create a customer managed key. Use the key to encrypt the EBS volumes.
options.B: Use an AWS managed key to encrypt the EBS volumes. Use the key to configure automatic key rotation.
options.C: Create an external KMS key with imported key material. Use the key to encrypt the EBS volumes.
options.D: Use an AWS owned key to encrypt the EBS volumes.

explanations.correct:
KMS is AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) allows you to create and manage cryptographic keys and control their use across a wide range of AWS services.

To address the requirements in this scenario, utilizing KMS is the optimal choice. This solution is designed for encrypting data at rest, managing encryption keys, and integrating seamlessly with services like EBS, S3, and RDS. This aligns with the goal of Security and ensures the architecture is robust and follows AWS best practices.

Hence, the correct answer is: Create a customer managed key. Use the key to encrypt the EBS volumes.
explanations.B: The option that says: 'Use an AWS managed key to encrypt the EBS volumes. Use the key to configure automatic key rotation.' is incorrect. EBS is Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) provides block level storage volumes for use with EC2 instances. typically used for persistent block storage for databases, file systems, and applications running on EC2 instances. In this specific context, it is not the right fit because EBS volumes are AZ-locked and must be attached to an instance; S3 is better for regional object storage. The scenario is better served by the capabilities of KMS.
explanations.C: The option that says: 'Create an external KMS key with imported key material. Use the key to encrypt the EBS volumes.' is incorrect. While this option mentions KMS, the specific configuration is not ideal. KMS manages keys; it is not a certificate authority (use ACM for TLS certificates). The proposed method may introduce operational overhead or fail to meet the specific requirements of the scenario.
explanations.D: The option that says: 'Use an AWS owned key to encrypt the EBS volumes.' is incorrect. EBS is Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) provides block level storage volumes for use with EC2 instances. typically used for persistent block storage for databases, file systems, and applications running on EC2 instances. In this specific context, it is not the right fit because EBS volumes are AZ-locked and must be attached to an instance; S3 is better for regional object storage. The scenario is better served by the capabilities of KMS.

questions.text: A company is building a game system that needs to send unique events to separate leaderboard, matchmaking, and authentication services concurrently. The company needs an AWS event-driven system that guarantees the order of the events. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Amazon EventBridge event bus
options.B: Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) FIFO topics
options.C: Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) standard topics
options.D: Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queues

explanations.A: Amazon EventBridge does not guarantee the order in which events are delivered to targets.
explanations.B: SNS FIFO topics allow for message 'fan-out' (sending to multiple subscribers) while maintaining strict ordering and deduplication, which fulfills both the concurrent delivery and ordering requirements.
explanations.C: Standard SNS topics do not guarantee message ordering; they follow a best-effort approach.
explanations.D: While SQS FIFO guarantees order, it is designed for a 'one-to-one' delivery model (point-to-point) rather than the 'one-to-many' fan-out required for multiple concurrent services.
explanations.correct: SNS FIFO topics provide the ordering guarantee needed for event-driven architectures that require fan-out to multiple subscribers.

questions.text: A company needs to store its accounting records in Amazon S3. The records must be immediately accessible for 1 year and then must be archived for an additional 9 years. No one at the company, including administrative users and root users, can be able to delete the records during the entire 10-year period. The records must be stored with maximum resiliency. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Store the records in S3 Glacier for the entire 10-year period. Use an access control policy to deny deletion of the records for a period of 10 years.
options.B: Store the records by using S3 Intelligent-Tiering. Use an IAM policy to deny deletion of the records. After 10 years, change the IAM policy to allow deletion.
options.C: Use an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the records from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year. Use S3 Object Lock in compliance mode for a period of 10 years.
options.D: Use an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition the records from S3 Standard to S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) after 1 year. Use S3 Object Lock in governance mode for a period of 10 years.

explanations.A: Standard S3 Glacier does not support immediate access for the first year. Access control policies (Bucket policies) can be modified by the root user or administrators, which fails the requirement.
explanations.B: IAM policies can be deleted or modified by users with administrative privileges or the root user. This provides no protection against accidental or malicious deletion by an admin.
explanations.C: S3 Object Lock in 'compliance mode' ensures that objects cannot be deleted by any user, including the root user. S3 Standard provides immediate access, and Glacier Deep Archive provides cost-effective, highly resilient long-term storage.
explanations.D: S3 One Zone-IA stores data in a single Availability Zone, which does not meet the 'maximum resiliency' requirement. Governance mode allows users with specific permissions to delete objects or change settings.
explanations.correct: S3 Object Lock Compliance mode is the only way to prevent even the root user from deleting objects. Combining it with S3 Standard and Glacier Deep Archive satisfies the access, cost, and resilience needs.

questions.text: A company has a regional streaming service on EC2 instances in Auto Scaling groups behind ELBs and an Amazon Aurora database. The company wants to expand globally and ensure minimal downtime with the MOST fault tolerance. Which solution will provide the MOST fault tolerance?

options.A: Extend the Auto Scaling groups for the web tier and the application tier to deploy instances in Availability Zones in a second Region. Use an Aurora global database to deploy the database in the primary Region and the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region.
options.B: Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Add an Aurora PostgreSQL cross-Region Aurora Replica in the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region. Promote the secondary to primary as needed.
options.C: Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Create an Aurora PostgreSQL database in the second Region. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to replicate the primary database to the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region.
options.D: Deploy the web tier and the application tier to a second Region. Use an Amazon Aurora global database to deploy the database in the primary Region and the second Region. Use Amazon Route 53 health checks with a failover routing policy to the second Region. Promote the secondary to primary as needed.

explanations.A: Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling groups are regional resources and cannot span multiple AWS Regions. This architecture is technically impossible to implement.
explanations.B: Promoting a standard cross-region replica is slower and more operationally complex than using Aurora Global Database, which is specifically designed for cross-region disaster recovery.
explanations.C: AWS DMS is a logical migration tool. Using it for live production database replication across regions for DR introduces significant latency and management overhead compared to physical storage-level replication.
explanations.D: Aurora Global Database provides low-latency cross-region replication and fast failover. Combined with separate application stacks in the target region and Route 53 DNS failover, it offers the most robust fault-tolerant architecture.
explanations.correct: Amazon Aurora Global Database is the purpose-built solution for multi-region resilience, providing the highest level of data durability and availability during regional outages.

questions.text: A data analytics company receives thousands of small files daily via FTP. A batch job currently takes hours to process them overnight. The company wants to process incoming files as soon as possible with minimal changes to the FTP clients. Each file takes 3-8 minutes to process. Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST operationally efficient way?

options.A: Use an Amazon EC2 instance that runs an FTP server to store incoming files as objects in Amazon S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch. Use Amazon EventBridge rules to invoke the job to process the objects nightly from S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval. Delete the objects after the job has processed the objects.
options.B: Use an Amazon EC2 instance that runs an FTP server to store incoming files on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch. Use Amazon EventBridge rules to invoke the job to process the files nightly from the EBS volume. Delete the files after the job has processed the files.
options.C: Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server to store incoming files on an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume. Configure a job queue in AWS Batch. Use an Amazon S3 event notification when each file arrives to invoke the job in AWS Batch. Delete the files after the job has processed the files.
options.D: Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server to store incoming files in Amazon S3 Standard. Create an AWS Lambda function to process the files and to delete the files after they are processed. Use an S3 event notification to invoke the Lambda function when the files arrive.

explanations.A: Glacier Flexible Retrieval introduces high retrieval latency, and hosting an FTP server on EC2 creates significant management overhead. Nightly batching fails the 'as soon as possible' requirement.
explanations.B: EBS volumes are not directly accessible by FTP clients without a server on EC2. Nightly processing does not meet the requirement for near-real-time ingestion.
explanations.C: AWS Transfer Family for FTP can integrate with S3 or EFS, but not EBS directly. AWS Batch is suited for larger batch workloads rather than immediate processing of single small files as they arrive.
explanations.D: AWS Transfer Family is a managed FTP service. Storing files in S3 triggers Lambda immediately. Lambda is capable of 3-8 minute processing, meeting all requirements with a serverless, low-maintenance architecture.
explanations.correct: The combination of AWS Transfer Family for managed ingestion and AWS Lambda for event-driven, serverless processing provides the most efficient and responsive solution.

questions.text: A company has an online gaming application that has TCP and UDP multiplayer gaming capabilities. The company uses Route 53 to point traffic to multiple Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in different AWS Regions. The company needs to improve performance and decrease latency for growth. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the NLBs. Increase the Cache-Control max-age parameter.
options.B: Replace the NLBs with Application Load Balancers (ALBs). Configure Route 53 to use latency-based routing.
options.C: Add AWS Global Accelerator in front of the NLBs. Configure a Global Accelerator endpoint to use the correct listener ports.
options.D: Add an Amazon API Gateway endpoint behind the NLBs. Enable API caching. Override method caching for the different stages.

explanations.A: CloudFront is optimized for HTTP/HTTPS traffic. While it has some support for custom origins, it is not the primary tool for reducing latency for generic TCP/UDP multiplayer game traffic.
explanations.B: Application Load Balancers (ALBs) operate at Layer 7 and do not support UDP traffic, which is critical for many multiplayer gaming applications.
explanations.C: AWS Global Accelerator uses the AWS global network to route traffic to the optimal regional endpoint. It supports TCP and UDP and provides static IP addresses, significantly improving performance and reducing jitter for global users.
explanations.D: API Gateway is an HTTP-based service and does not handle the TCP/UDP protocols required by the game engine.
explanations.correct: AWS Global Accelerator is specifically designed to improve availability and performance for global applications over TCP or UDP protocols by utilizing the AWS private network.

questions.text: A company needs to integrate with a third-party data feed. The data feed sends a webhook to notify an external service when new data is ready for consumption. A developer wrote an AWS Lambda function to retrieve data when the company receives a webhook callback. The developer must make the Lambda function available for the third party to call. Which solution will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

options.A: Create a function URL for the Lambda function. Provide the Lambda function URL to the third party for the webhook.
options.B: Deploy an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the Lambda function. Provide the ALB URL to the third party for the webhook.
options.C: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Attach the topic to the Lambda function. Provide the public hostname of the SNS topic to the third party for the webhook.
options.D: Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Attach the queue to the Lambda function. Provide the public hostname of the SQS queue to the third party for the webhook.

explanations.A: Lambda function URLs provide a dedicated HTTP(S) endpoint for a single Lambda function. This is the most operationally efficient solution because it requires no additional infrastructure (like API Gateway or ALB) and is managed directly through the Lambda configuration.
explanations.B: While an ALB can trigger a Lambda function, it involves provisioning and managing a load balancer, target groups, and potentially listeners/rules, which increases operational overhead compared to a function URL.
explanations.C: SNS is a pub/sub service. While it can trigger Lambda, third parties cannot typically post directly to an SNS topic 'hostname' via a standard webhook without using the AWS SDK/API, and it doesn't provide a simple URL endpoint.
explanations.D: SQS is a queuing service. Third parties cannot post webhooks directly to an SQS queue via standard HTTP without using the AWS SQS API or an intermediate service. It does not provide a public URL for standard webhook consumption.
explanations.correct: Lambda function URLs are a built-in feature designed for simple use cases like webhooks, offering a direct HTTPS endpoint with zero additional resource management.

questions.text: A company uses Amazon API Gateway to run a private gateway with two REST APIs in the same VPC. The BuyStock RESTful web service calls the CheckFunds RESTful web service to ensure that enough funds are available before a stock can be purchased. The company has noticed in the VPC flow logs that the BuyStock RESTful web service calls the CheckFunds RESTful web service over the internet instead of through the VPC. A solutions architect must implement a solution so that the APIs communicate through the VPC. Which solution will meet these requirements with the FEWEST changes to the code?

options.A: Add an X-API-Key header in the HTTP header for authorization.
options.B: Use an interface endpoint.
options.C: Use a gateway endpoint.
options.D: Add an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue between the two REST APIs.

explanations.A: API keys are used for identification and authorization, not for controlling the network routing path between services.
explanations.B: Interface VPC endpoints (powered by AWS PrivateLink) provide private connectivity to AWS services. Creating an interface endpoint for API Gateway allows the web services to communicate via private IP addresses within the VPC, keeping traffic off the public internet.
explanations.C: Gateway endpoints are exclusively for Amazon S3 and Amazon DynamoDB. They cannot be used for API Gateway REST APIs.
explanations.D: Implementing SQS would require significant architectural and code changes to move from a synchronous REST call to an asynchronous message-based workflow, violating the requirement for fewest code changes.
explanations.correct: Interface endpoints are the standard mechanism for private communication with API Gateway from within a VPC without traversing the internet.

questions.text: A company hosts a multiplayer gaming application on AWS. The company wants the application to read data with sub-millisecond latency and run one-time queries on historical data. Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use Amazon RDS for data that is frequently accessed. Run a periodic custom script to export the data to an Amazon S3 bucket.
options.B: Store the data directly in an Amazon S3 bucket. Implement an S3 Lifecycle policy to move older data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive for long-term storage. Run one-time queries on the data in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Athena.
options.C: Use Amazon DynamoDB with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for data that is frequently accessed. Export the data to an Amazon S3 bucket by using DynamoDB table export. Run one-time queries on the data in Amazon S3 by using Amazon Athena.
options.D: Use Amazon DynamoDB for data that is frequently accessed. Turn on streaming to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to read the data from Kinesis Data Streams. Store the records in an Amazon S3 bucket.

explanations.A: RDS provides single-digit millisecond latency, which does not meet the sub-millisecond requirement. Custom scripts also increase operational overhead.
explanations.B: S3 read latency is significantly higher than sub-millisecond requirements for gaming applications.
explanations.C: DAX provides sub-millisecond latency for DynamoDB reads. The native 'Export to S3' feature handles the data movement for historical analysis with minimal management, and Athena provides serverless querying.
explanations.D: While this works, managing Kinesis Data Streams and Firehose involves more operational overhead than the native DynamoDB export feature provided in Option C.
explanations.correct: DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is specifically designed for sub-millisecond response times, and DynamoDB export to S3 is the most managed path for historical querying with Athena.

questions.text: A company uses a payment processing system that requires messages for a particular payment ID to be received in the same order that they were sent. Otherwise, the payments might be processed incorrectly. Which actions should a solutions architect take to meet this requirement? (Choose two.)

options.A: Write the messages to an Amazon DynamoDB table with the payment ID as the partition key.
options.B: Write the messages to an Amazon Kinesis data stream with the payment ID as the partition key.
options.C: Write the messages to an Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached cluster with the payment ID as the key.
options.D: Write the messages to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Set the message attribute to use the payment ID.
options.E: Write the messages to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) FIFO queue. Set the message group to use the payment ID.

explanations.A: DynamoDB is a database and does not guarantee the delivery order of change events to a consumer without additional complex logic.
explanations.B: Kinesis Data Streams maintain strict ordering within a shard. By using the payment ID as the partition key, all messages for that ID are routed to the same shard, preserving the sequence.
explanations.C: ElastiCache is a cache and does not provide an ordered messaging or queuing mechanism.
explanations.D: Standard SQS queues provide best-effort ordering but do not guarantee strict sequential delivery.
explanations.E: SQS FIFO (First-In-First-Out) queues are designed to preserve the order of messages. The Message Group ID (payment ID) ensures messages in that group are processed sequentially.
explanations.correct: Kinesis and SQS FIFO are the two primary AWS services used for maintaining strict message ordering based on a sequence or key.

questions.text: A company has a workload in an AWS Region. Customers connect to and access the workload by using an Amazon API Gateway REST API. The company uses Amazon Route 53 as its DNS provider. The company wants to provide individual and secure URLs for all customers. Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency? (Choose three.)

options.A: Register the required domain in a registrar. Create a wildcard custom domain name in a Route 53 hosted zone and record in the zone that points to the API Gateway endpoint.
options.B: Request a wildcard certificate that matches the domains in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in a different Region.
options.C: Create hosted zones for each customer as required in Route 53. Create zone records that point to the API Gateway endpoint.
options.D: Request a wildcard certificate that matches the custom domain name in AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) in the same Region.
options.E: Create multiple API endpoints for each customer in API Gateway.
options.F: Create a custom domain name in API Gateway for the REST API. Import the certificate from AWS Certificate Manager (ACM).

explanations.A: Creating a wildcard record (e.g., *.example.com) in Route 53 allows the company to support any number of customer subdomains with a single DNS entry, minimizing management effort.
explanations.B: Certificates for Regional API Gateway endpoints must be requested in the same Region as the API, not a different Region.
explanations.C: Creating individual hosted zones for every customer represents extreme operational overhead and is not scalable compared to a single wildcard zone.
explanations.D: A wildcard certificate (e.g., *.example.com) in ACM allows for secure HTTPS connections across all customer subdomains. For a Regional endpoint, the ACM certificate must be in the same Region.

questions.text: A company recently launched a variety of new workloads on Amazon EC2 instances in its AWS account. options.A: Use the EC2 serial console to directly access the terminal interface of each instance for administration.
options.B: Attach the appropriate IAM role to each existing instance and new instance. Use AWS Systems Manager Session Manager to establish a remote SSH session.
options.C: Create an administrative SSH key pair. Load the public key into each EC2 instance. Deploy a bastion host in a public subnet to provide a tunnel for administration of each instance.
options.D: Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. Instruct administrators to use their local on-premises machines to connect directly to the instances by using SSH keys across the VPN tunnel.

explanations.A: The EC2 Serial Console is intended for troubleshooting boot and network configuration issues, not for routine administration of multiple instances.
explanations.B: Session Manager is a fully managed service that provides secure instance management without the need for bastion hosts, open inbound ports, or SSH key management. It uses IAM for authorization and provides an audit trail through CloudTrail and S3/CloudWatch Logs.
explanations.C: Deploying a bastion host introduces significant operational overhead, including managing the host's lifecycle, securing it, and managing SSH keys across all instances.
explanations.D: A VPN connection requires significant setup and ongoing maintenance of networking infrastructure. It does not natively provide the auditability and granular access control of Session Manager.
explanations.correct: AWS Systems Manager Session Manager is the recommended native solution for secure, keyless, and auditable remote access with the lowest operational overhead.

questions.text: A company needs to create an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster to host a digital media streaming application. options.A: Use a Kubernetes plugin that uses the customer managed key to perform data encryption.
options.B: After creation of the EKS cluster, locate the EBS volumes. Enable encryption by using the customer managed key.
options.C: Enable EBS encryption by default in the AWS Region where the EKS cluster will be created. Select the customer managed key as the default key.
options.D: Create the EKS cluster. Create an IAM role that has a policy that grants permission to the customer managed key. Associate the role with the EKS cluster.
options.E: Store the customer managed key as a Kubernetes secret in the EKS cluster. Use the customer managed key to encrypt the EBS volumes.

explanations.A: Using a custom plugin increases operational overhead and complexity compared to using native AWS encryption features.
explanations.B: Existing EBS volumes cannot be encrypted in place. This would require snapshots and recreation, leading to high operational overhead.
explanations.C: Enabling EBS encryption by default at the regional level ensures that all new volumes created for the EKS nodes are automatically encrypted with the specified customer managed key with zero manual intervention per volume.
explanations.D: The IAM role associated with the EKS cluster and nodes must have specific permissions (kms:CreateGrant, kms:Decrypt, etc.) to allow the EBS service to use the customer managed key for encryption and decryption.
explanations.E: KMS keys cannot be 'stored' as secrets in Kubernetes. This is a security anti-pattern and technically incorrect for EBS volume encryption.
explanations.correct: Regional EBS encryption by default (Option C) ensures all volumes are covered, while Option D provides the necessary cryptographic permissions for the infrastructure to perform the encryption.

questions.text: A company has an application that collects data from IoT sensors on automobiles. The data is streamed and stored in Amazon S3 through Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. The data produces trillions of S3 objects each year. Each morning, the company uses the data from the previous 30 days to retrain machine learning (ML) models. Four times each year, the company uses the previous 12 months of data for analysis. The data must be available with minimal delay for up to 1 year. After 1 year, the data must be retained for archival purposes. Which storage solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Use the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year.
options.B: Use the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class. Configure S3 Intelligent-Tiering to automatically move objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year.
options.C: Use the S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year.
options.D: Use the S3 Standard storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition objects to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 30 days, and then to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 year.

explanations.A: S3 Intelligent-Tiering has a monthly monitoring and automation charge per object. With trillions of objects, this fee would be extremely high, making it less cost-effective than a deterministic lifecycle policy when the access pattern is known.
explanations.B: Similar to Option A, the automation charges for trillions of objects are prohibitive. Furthermore, S3 Intelligent-Tiering's archive tiers are optional and intended for unpredictable patterns, which does not apply here.
explanations.C: S3 Standard-IA has a minimum storage duration charge of 30 days and retrieval fees. Using it for the first 30 days while data is accessed daily for retraining would result in high retrieval costs.
explanations.D: This aligns with the known access pattern: S3 Standard for the first 30 days (frequent daily access), S3 Standard-IA for the remainder of the year (infrequent quarterly analysis with minimal delay requirement), and Glacier Deep Archive for long-term storage (archival). This avoids S3 Intelligent-Tiering automation fees for a massive number of objects.
explanations.correct: When access patterns are predictable and the object count is extremely high (trillions), a manually defined Lifecycle policy using Standard and Standard-IA is more cost-effective than Intelligent-Tiering due to the lack of per-object automation fees.

questions.text: A company wants to migrate an Oracle database to AWS. The database consists of a single table containing millions of high-resolution GIS images identified by geographic codes. When a natural disaster occurs, tens of thousands of images are updated every few minutes. Each code has one associated image. The solution must be highly available, scalable, and cost-effective. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Store the images and geographic codes in a database table. Use Oracle running on an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance.
options.B: Store the images in Amazon S3 buckets. Use Amazon DynamoDB with the geographic code as the key and the image S3 URL as the value.
options.C: Store the images and geographic codes in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Configure DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) during times of high load.
options.D: Store the images in Amazon S3 buckets. Store geographic codes and image S3 URLs in a database table. Use Oracle running on an Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance.

explanations.A: Storing large binary objects (BLOBs) directly in a relational database like Oracle is expensive, hinders performance, and makes scaling difficult and costly.
explanations.B: Amazon S3 is the most cost-effective and scalable service for storing large image files. DynamoDB provides a serverless, highly available key-value store that handles high write throughput (tens of thousands of updates) better and cheaper than a relational database for a single-table schema.
explanations.C: DynamoDB has a 400 KB item size limit, which GIS images likely exceed. DAX is a cache for reads and does not help with the high volume of writes/updates described.
explanations.D: While this offloads images to S3, maintaining an Oracle RDS instance for a single-table key-value lookup is significantly more expensive than DynamoDB due to licensing and instance costs.
explanations.correct: The combination of S3 for bulk data and DynamoDB for metadata is a classic AWS design pattern for high-scale, cost-effective performance.

questions.text: A company runs a web application that is backed by Amazon RDS. A new database administrator caused data loss by accidentally editing information in a database table. To help recover from this type of incident, the company wants the ability to restore the database to its state from 5 minutes before any change within the last 30 days. Which feature should the solutions architect include in the design to meet this requirement?

options.A: Read replicas
options.B: Manual snapshots
options.C: Automated backups
options.D: Multi-AZ deployments

explanations.A: Read replicas are used for read scalability and some disaster recovery, but they replicate changes (including accidental edits/deletions) almost immediately, making them unsuitable for point-in-time recovery of data errors.
explanations.B: Manual snapshots are taken by the user and do not support point-in-time recovery (PITR) to a specific second. They only allow restoration to the exact moment the snapshot was taken.
explanations.C: Automated backups enable point-in-time recovery (PITR). Amazon RDS captures transaction logs and uploads them to S3 every 5 minutes, allowing a restore to any point in time within the retention period (up to 35 days), down to a specific second.
explanations.D: Multi-AZ deployments provide high availability and failover support at the infrastructure level, but they synchronously replicate data changes. An accidental edit on the primary is immediately reflected on the standby.
explanations.correct: Automated backups are the native RDS feature that enables Point-in-Time Recovery (PITR), which is the specific requirement for restoring to a state just before a human error occurred.

questions.text: A company’s web application consists of an Amazon API Gateway API in front of an AWS Lambda function and an Amazon DynamoDB database. explanations.A: Caching and throttling improve performance and protect against traffic spikes but do not provide authorization logic based on user subscriptions.
explanations.B: AWS WAF is used for web security (SQLi, XSS) and IP filtering. It is not intended for managing application-level subscription logic or user-based authorization.
explanations.C: Fine-grained IAM for DynamoDB is complex to manage at scale for end-users and requires mapping Cognito identities to specific IAM policies, resulting in high operational overhead.
explanations.D: API Gateway usage plans and API keys are the standard managed way to provide different tiers of access (e.g., basic vs. premium) with specific quotas and throttling limits, minimizing custom code and management effort.
explanations.correct: Usage plans and API keys allow the architect to bundle APIs into different products and manage access tiers effectively with native API Gateway features.

questions.text: A solutions architect wants all new users to have specific complexity requirements and mandatory rotation periods for IAM user passwords. What should the solutions architect do to accomplish this?

options.A: Set an overall password policy for the entire AWS account.
options.B: Set a password policy for each IAM user in the AWS account.
options.C: Use third-party vendor software to set password requirements.
options.D: Attach an Amazon CloudWatch rule to the Create_newuser event to set the password with the appropriate requirements.

explanations.A: The IAM account password policy is a global setting that defines requirements (length, complexity, rotation) for all IAM users within that AWS account.
explanations.B: AWS does not support setting individual password policies on a per-user basis; it is managed at the account level.
explanations.C: Third-party software is unnecessary as AWS provides this capability natively through IAM.
explanations.D: This is an over-engineered approach. CloudWatch (EventBridge) and Lambda could theoretically intercept events, but it significantly increases operational overhead compared to a native policy.
explanations.correct: The account-level password policy is the standard, least-overhead method to enforce security standards for IAM user credentials.

questions.text: A company uses Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing for a UDP-based application hosted on redundant on-premises servers in the US, Asia, and Europe. Compliance requires the app remain on-premises. The company wants to improve performance and availability. What should a solutions architect do?

options.A: Configure three Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in the three AWS Regions to address the on-premises endpoints. Create an accelerator by using AWS Global Accelerator, and register the NLBs as its endpoints. Provide access to the application by using a CNAME that points to the accelerator DNS.
options.B: Configure three Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in the three AWS Regions to address the on-premises endpoints. Create an accelerator by using AWS Global Accelerator, and register the ALBs as its endpoints. Provide access to the application by using a CNAME that points to the accelerator DNS.
options.C: Configure three Network Load Balancers (NLBs) in the three AWS Regions to address the on-premises endpoints. In Route 53, create a latency-based record that points to the three NLBs, and use it as an origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Provide access to the application by using a CNAME that points to the CloudFront DNS.
options.D: Configure three Application Load Balancers (ALBs) in the three AWS Regions to address the on-premises endpoints. In Route 53, create a latency-based record that points to the three ALBs, and use it as an origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Provide access to the application by using a CNAME that points to the CloudFront DNS.

explanations.A: AWS Global Accelerator provides Anycast IP addresses and routes traffic over the AWS global network, which is ideal for improving UDP performance. NLBs support UDP and can target on-premises IP addresses via Direct Connect or VPN.
explanations.B: ALBs operate at Layer 7 and only support HTTP/HTTPS and gRPC; they do not support UDP.
explanations.C: Amazon CloudFront is a Content Delivery Network primarily for HTTP/HTTPS traffic. It does not support UDP traffic.
explanations.D: This combines two unsupported elements for this use case: ALBs and CloudFront do not support the UDP protocol requirement.
explanations.correct: The combination of Global Accelerator and NLB is the standard AWS architectural pattern for optimizing non-HTTP (TCP/UDP) traffic globally.

questions.text: A company migrated an application to EC2 Linux. One instance runs several 1-hour tasks on a schedule written in different languages. The company is concerned about performance and scalability on a single instance. Which solution resolves this with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.A: Use AWS Batch to run the tasks as jobs. Schedule the jobs by using Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events).
options.B: Convert the EC2 instance to a container. Use AWS App Runner to create the container on demand to run the tasks as jobs.
options.C: Copy the tasks into AWS Lambda functions. Schedule the Lambda functions by using Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events).
options.D: Create an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) of the EC2 instance that runs the tasks. Create an Auto Scaling group with the AMI to run multiple copies of the instance.

explanations.A: AWS Batch is designed for batch computing and can handle tasks of varying durations and languages. It automatically scales compute resources based on the job queue, providing high performance and scalability without manual server management.
explanations.B: AWS App Runner is primarily for long-running web services and APIs, not for scheduling individual batch jobs that run for an hour.
explanations.C: AWS Lambda has a maximum execution timeout of 15 minutes (900 seconds). It cannot support the 1-hour tasks described in the scenario.
explanations.D: Using an Auto Scaling group with an AMI of the full instance is inefficient. It would launch entire servers just to run individual tasks, leading to high operational overhead and wasted costs.
explanations.correct: AWS Batch is the most suitable managed service for running scheduled, long-running (1 hour+) batch jobs that require varied programming environments.

questions.text: A company hosts a frontend application that uses an Amazon API Gateway API backend that is integrated with AWS Lambda. When the API receives requests, the Lambda function loads many libraries. Then the Lambda function connects to an Amazon RDS database, processes the data, and returns the data to the frontend application. The company wants to ensure that response latency is as low as possible for all its users with the fewest number of changes to the company's operations. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Establish a connection between the frontend application and the database to make queries faster by bypassing the API.
options.B: Configure provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function that handles the requests.
options.C: Cache the results of the queries in Amazon S3 for faster retrieval of similar datasets.
options.D: Increase the size of the database to increase the number of connections Lambda can establish at one time.

explanations.A: Bypassing the API Gateway and Lambda to connect directly from a frontend (likely client-side) to a database is a significant security risk and would require massive architectural changes, violating the requirement for 'fewest changes'.
explanations.B: Provisioned concurrency keeps Lambda functions initialized and ready to respond in double-digit milliseconds. Since the function 'loads many libraries', it likely suffers from high 'cold start' latency. Provisioned concurrency eliminates this by pre-loading the execution environment and libraries.
explanations.C: While caching can reduce latency, using Amazon S3 as a cache for API results is slower than other caching methods (like API Gateway caching) and requires code changes to implement logic for S3 puts/gets.
explanations.D: Increasing database size helps with throughput and connection limits, but it does not address the application-tier latency caused by Lambda library loading and initialization.
explanations.correct: Provisioned concurrency is the standard AWS solution for reducing 'cold start' latency in Lambda functions that have heavy initialization logic or large deployment packages.

questions.text: A company is hosting a static website on Amazon S3 and is using Amazon Route 53 for DNS. The website is experiencing increased demand from around the world. The company must decrease latency for users who access the website. Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Replicate the S3 bucket that contains the website to all AWS Regions. Add Route 53 geolocation routing entries.
options.B: Provision accelerators in AWS Global Accelerator. Associate the supplied IP addresses with the S3 bucket. Edit the Route 53 entries to point to the IP addresses of the accelerators.
options.C: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the S3 bucket. Edit the Route 53 entries to point to the CloudFront distribution.
options.D: Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the bucket. Edit the Route 53 entries to point to the new endpoint.

explanations.A: S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) to all regions is expensive due to storage costs for multiple copies and inter-region data transfer fees. It also adds significant management overhead.
explanations.B: Global Accelerator is generally used for TCP/UDP traffic to improve availability. While it can reduce latency, it is not optimized for static content delivery compared to a CDN and is more expensive for this use case.
explanations.C: Amazon CloudFront is a Content Delivery Network (CDN) designed specifically to cache static content at edge locations close to users worldwide. It is the most cost-effective way to reduce latency for S3-hosted static sites and often reduces data egress costs from S3.
explanations.D: S3 Transfer Acceleration is designed to speed up uploads (PUTs) to S3 over long distances, not to optimize global read performance for website visitors.
explanations.correct: CloudFront is the native AWS CDN service and is the best-practice choice for global distribution of static content stored in S3.

questions.text: A company is migrating its on-premises workload to the AWS Cloud. The company already uses several Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon RDS DB instances. The company wants a solution that automatically starts and stops the EC2 instances and DB instances outside of business hours. The solution must minimize cost and infrastructure maintenance. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Scale the EC2 instances by using elastic resize. Scale the DB instances to zero outside of business hours.
options.B: Explore AWS Marketplace for partner solutions that will automatically start and stop the EC2 instances and DB instances on a schedule.
options.C: Launch another EC2 instance. Configure a crontab schedule to run shell scripts that will start and stop the existing EC2 instances and DB instances on a schedule.
options.D: Create an AWS Lambda function that will start and stop the EC2 instances and DB instances. Configure Amazon EventBridge to invoke the Lambda function on a schedule.

explanations.A: RDS DB instances cannot be scaled to 'zero' while maintaining the instance configuration. You must stop the instance to avoid compute charges, and 'elastic resize' is not a standard term for scheduled on/off scaling.
explanations.B: Partner solutions from the Marketplace usually incur third-party licensing costs or additional management, which does not minimize cost compared to native AWS serverless options.
explanations.C: Launching an EC2 instance to manage other instances introduces 'infrastructure maintenance' (patching, monitoring the management server) and incurs 24/7 compute costs for that management instance.
explanations.D: AWS Lambda is serverless (no maintenance) and has a generous free tier (low cost). EventBridge (CloudWatch Events) provides a native, managed cron-like scheduling mechanism to trigger the Lambda functions.
explanations.correct: The Lambda + EventBridge pattern is the standard serverless architectural approach for automated resource management on a schedule with minimal overhead.

questions.text: A company hosts a three-tier web application that includes a PostgreSQL database. The database stores metadata from documents stored in Amazon S3. The documents are updated frequently. The reporting process takes a few hours using relational queries but must not prevent document modifications or new additions. A solutions architect needs to implement a solution to speed up the reporting process with the LEAST amount of change to the application code. Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.A: Set up a new Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) cluster that includes a read replica. Scale the read replica to generate the reports.
options.B: Set up a new Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster that includes an Aurora Replica. Issue queries to the Aurora Replica to generate the reports.
options.C: Set up a new Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Multi-AZ DB instance. Configure the reporting module to query the secondary RDS node so that the reporting module does not affect the primary node.
options.D: Set up a new Amazon DynamoDB table to store the documents. Use a fixed write capacity to support new document entries. Automatically scale the read capacity to support the reports.

explanations.A: DocumentDB is a NoSQL database. Migrating from PostgreSQL to DocumentDB would require significant code changes to handle the non-relational data model and query language, violating the 'least change' requirement.
explanations.B: Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL is fully compatible with PostgreSQL, ensuring minimal code changes. Aurora Replicas share the same underlying storage as the primary instance and are specifically designed to handle read-heavy workloads (like reporting) without impacting the write performance of the primary instance.
explanations.C: In an RDS Multi-AZ configuration, the secondary instance is a standby node used for high availability and failover. It does not accept read connections. To offload reads in RDS, one must use Read Replicas, not the Multi-AZ secondary node.
explanations.D: DynamoDB is a NoSQL database. Moving from a relational PostgreSQL schema to DynamoDB would require a complete rewrite of the application's data access layer and reporting queries.
explanations.correct: Aurora Replicas provide a dedicated endpoint for read-only queries, allowing long-running reports to execute without competing for resources with the primary write instance, while maintaining full PostgreSQL compatibility.

questions.text: A company has a three-tier application on AWS that ingests sensor data through a Network Load Balancer (NLB), then to Amazon EC2 instances for the web tier, and finally to EC2 instances for the application tier. What should a solutions architect do to improve the security of the data in transit?

options.A: Configure a TLS listener. Deploy the server certificate on the NLB.
options.B: Configure AWS Shield Advanced. Enable AWS WAF on the NLB.
options.C: Change the load balancer to an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Enable AWS WAF on the ALB.
options.D: Encrypt the Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume on the EC2 instances by using AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS).

explanations.A: TLS (Transport Layer Security) is the standard protocol for securing data in transit. NLB supports TLS listeners, allowing the load balancer to handle the encryption/decryption (TLS termination) using a certificate, ensuring data is encrypted as it moves from the client to the load balancer.
explanations.B: AWS Shield Advanced is for DDoS protection, and AWS WAF is a web application firewall. Neither of these services provides encryption for data in transit.
explanations.C: While ALB supports AWS WAF, WAF is used for filtering malicious traffic (Layer 7), not for providing encryption. Furthermore, changing the load balancer type might not be necessary if the core requirement is transit security.
explanations.D: EBS encryption using KMS secures 'data at rest' on the disk. It does not provide security for data moving across the network between tiers.
explanations.correct: Configuring a TLS listener on the NLB ensures that the communication channel between the user devices and the AWS infrastructure is encrypted, directly addressing the requirement for data in transit security.

questions.text: A company is planning to migrate a commercial off-the-shelf application from its on-premises data center to AWS. The software has a software licensing model using sockets and cores with predictable capacity and uptime requirements. The company wants to use its existing licenses, which were purchased earlier this year. Which Amazon EC2 pricing option is the MOST cost-effective?

options.A: Dedicated Reserved Hosts
options.B: Dedicated On-Demand Hosts
options.C: Dedicated Reserved Instances
options.D: Dedicated On-Demand Instances

explanations.A: Dedicated Hosts are required to support Bring Your Own License (BYOL) scenarios for software licensed by physical sockets or cores. Since the capacity requirements are 'predictable', a 'Reserved' pricing model provides the maximum discount compared to On-Demand.
explanations.B: While On-Demand Dedicated Hosts support the licensing requirement, they are more expensive than Reserved Hosts for predictable workloads with high uptime requirements.
explanations.C: Dedicated Instances run on single-tenant hardware but do not provide the visibility or control over physical sockets and cores required for this specific licensing model.
explanations.D: Dedicated Instances do not provide the hardware visibility needed for socket-based licensing and are more expensive than reserved options for steady-state workloads.
explanations.correct: Dedicated Hosts are the only option that allows visibility into physical sockets and cores for licensing compliance, and the 'Reserved' offering provides the lowest cost for predictable uptime.

questions.text: A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 Linux instances across multiple Availability Zones. The application needs a storage layer that is highly available and POSIX-compliant. The storage layer must provide maximum data durability and must be shareable across the EC2 instances. The data will be accessed frequently for 30 days and infrequently thereafter. Which solution is MOST cost-effective?

options.A: Use the Amazon S3 Standard storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move infrequently accessed data to S3 Glacier.
options.B: Use the Amazon S3 Standard storage class. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move infrequently accessed data to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA).
options.C: Use the Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) Standard storage class. Create a lifecycle management policy to move infrequently accessed data to EFS Standard-Infrequent Access (EFS Standard-IA).
options.D: Use the Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) One Zone storage class. Create a lifecycle management policy to move infrequently accessed data to EFS One Zone-Infrequent Access (EFS One Zone-IA).

explanations.A: Amazon S3 is object storage and is not POSIX-compliant, failing the primary technical requirement for the application's storage layer.
explanations.B: S3 Standard-IA remains non-POSIX compliant and cannot be mounted as a standard file system for the Linux instances as required.
explanations.C: Amazon EFS is POSIX-compliant and shareable across instances. The Standard storage class replicates data across multiple AZs for 'maximum durability' and high availability. Lifecycle management to EFS-IA optimizes cost for data not accessed after 30 days.
explanations.D: EFS One Zone storage class stores data in a single AZ, failing the requirement for 'maximum data durability' and potentially causing availability issues for instances in other AZs.
explanations.correct: EFS Standard with Lifecycle Management provides the necessary POSIX compliance and Multi-AZ availability while automatically reducing costs for infrequently accessed data.

questions.text: A company has an application that ingests incoming messages. Dozens of other applications and microservicesthen quickly consume these messages. The number of messages varies drastically and sometimes increasessuddenly to 100,000 each second. The company wants to decouple the solution and increase scalability. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Persist the messages to Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics. Configure the consumer applications to read andprocess the messages.
options.B: Deploy the ingestion application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group to scale the number ofEC2 instances based on CPU metrics.
options.C: Write the messages to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with a single shard. Use an AWS Lambda function topreprocess messages and store them in Amazon DynamoDB. Configure the consumer applications to readfrom DynamoDB to process the messages.
options.D: Publish the messages to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic with multiple AmazonSimple Queue Service (Amazon SOS) subscriptions. Configure the consumer applications to process the

explanations.correct:
General is This refers to general AWS architectural best practices.

To address the requirements in this scenario, utilizing General is the optimal choice. This solution is designed for optimizing for one of the pillars of the Well-Architected Framework: Security, Reliability, Performance, or Cost. This aligns with the goal of General and ensures the architecture is robust and follows AWS best practices.

Hence, the correct answer is: Publish the messages to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic with multiple AmazonSimple Queue Service (Amazon SOS) subscriptions. Configure the consumer applications to process the
explanations.A: The option that says: 'Persist the messages to Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics. Configure the consumer applications to read andprocess the messages.' is incorrect. Kinesis is Amazon Kinesis makes it easy to collect, process, and analyze real-time, streaming data. typically used for ingesting real-time data streams (logs, IoT telemetry) for immediate analytics. In this specific context, it is not the right fit because Kinesis processes streams; SQS processes messages. Kinesis allows multiple consumers to read the same data; SQS deletes it after reading. The scenario is better served by the capabilities of General.
explanations.B: The option that says: 'Deploy the ingestion application on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group to scale the number ofEC2 instances based on CPU metrics.' is incorrect. Auto Scaling is AWS Auto Scaling monitors your applications and automatically adjusts capacity to maintain steady, predictable performance. typically used for matching supply with demand, ensuring high availability by replacing failed instances, and optimizing costs by scaling in. In this specific context, it is not the right fit because Auto Scaling manages capacity; it does not distribute traffic (that is the Load Balancer's job). The scenario is better served by the capabilities of General.
explanations.C: The option that says: 'Write the messages to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams with a single shard. Use an AWS Lambda function topreprocess messages and store them in Amazon DynamoDB. Configure the consumer applications to readfrom DynamoDB to process the messages.' is incorrect. DynamoDB is Amazon DynamoDB is a fully managed, serverless, key-value NoSQL database designed to run high-performance applications at any scale. typically used for applications requiring single-digit millisecond latency, unlimited throughput, and massive scale (e.g., gaming leaderboards, shopping carts). In this specific context, it is not the right fit because DynamoDB does not support complex SQL joins or ad-hoc analytics as effectively as RDS or Redshift. The scenario is better served by the capabilities of General.

questions.text: A solutions architect is creating a new VPC design with public subnets for a load balancer, private subnets for web servers, and private subnets for MySQL. The load balancer security group allows port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. Which additional configuration strategy meets the requirement of least privilege access?

options.A: Create a security group for the web servers and allow port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. Create a security group for the MySQL servers and allow port 3306 from the web servers security group.
options.B: Create a network ACL for the web servers and allow port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0. Create a network ACL for the MySQL servers and allow port 3306 from the web servers security group.
options.C: Create a security group for the web servers and allow port 443 from the load balancer. Create a security group for the MySQL servers and allow port 3306 from the web servers security group.
options.D: Create a network ACL for the web servers and allow port 443 from the load balancer. Create a network ACL for the MySQL servers and allow port 3306 from the web servers security group.

explanations.A: Allowing port 443 from 0.0.0.0/0 on the web servers is not least privilege; they should only receive traffic from the load balancer, not the entire internet.
explanations.B: Network ACLs are stateless and apply at the subnet level. They cannot reference security groups, making the database rule technically impossible as described.
explanations.C: Referencing security groups in rules (chaining) is the best practice for least privilege. The web servers only accept traffic from the ALB's security group, and the DB only accepts traffic from the web server security group.
explanations.D: Network ACLs are coarse-grained and do not support security group references as sources/destinations. Security groups are the correct tool for instance-level least privilege.
explanations.correct: Chaining security groups ensures that only traffic originating from specific application tiers can reach the next tier, effectively implementing a zero-trust approach within the VPC.

questions.text: A new deployment engineer will be using AWS CloudFormation templates to create multiple AWS resources. A solutions architect wants the engineer to follow the principle of least privilege. Which combination of actions should the solutions architect take? (Choose two.)

options.A: Have the deployment engineer use AWS account root user credentials for performing AWS CloudFormation stack operations.
options.B: Create a new IAM user for the deployment engineer and add the IAM user to a group that has the PowerUsers IAM policy attached.
options.C: Create a new IAM user for the deployment engineer and add the IAM user to a group that has the AdministratorAccess IAM policy attached.
options.D: Create a new IAM user for the deployment engineer and add the IAM user to a group that has an IAM policy that allows AWS CloudFormation actions only.
options.E: Create an IAM role for the deployment engineer to explicitly define the permissions specific to the AWS CloudFormation stack and launch stacks using that IAM role.

explanations.A: Root user credentials should never be used for daily tasks. This provides complete control and violates least privilege.
explanations.B: The PowerUsers policy is overly permissive, granting wide-ranging access to many AWS services beyond what is needed for CloudFormation management.
explanations.C: AdministratorAccess provides full access to the account, which is the opposite of the principle of least privilege.
explanations.D: Creating an IAM user with a policy restricted to CloudFormation actions ensures the user can only interact with the service needed for their job function.
explanations.E: CloudFormation Service Roles allow you to define exactly what resources the stack is allowed to create or modify, ensuring that the service itself operates under restricted permissions.
explanations.correct: Restricting the user to CloudFormation actions (D) and using a service role for the stack itself (E) ensures a layered approach to least privilege.

questions.text: An ecommerce company is running a multi-tier application on AWS. The front-end and backend tiers both run on EC2, and the database runs on Amazon RDS for MySQL. Frequent calls for identical datasets are causing performance slowdowns. Which action should be taken to improve performance?

options.A: Implement Amazon SNS to store the database calls.
options.B: Implement Amazon ElastiCache to cache the large datasets.
options.C: Implement an RDS for MySQL read replica to cache database calls.
options.D: Implement Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to stream the calls to the database.

explanations.A: Amazon SNS is a notification service and cannot store or cache database query results.
explanations.B: Amazon ElastiCache (Redis or Memcached) provides an in-memory data store that can cache identical query results, significantly reducing latency and offloading traffic from the primary RDS instance.
explanations.C: Read replicas help with read scaling by distributing traffic, but they are still disk-based relational databases and do not provide the sub-millisecond latency of an in-memory cache.
explanations.D: Kinesis Data Firehose is for streaming data ingestion into destinations like S3 or Redshift; it is not a solution for accelerating database query performance.
explanations.correct: Caching 'identical datasets' is a classic use case for an in-memory store like ElastiCache to optimize application response times.

questions.text: A company hosts a multi-tier web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The instances run in an Auto Scaling group across multiple Availability Zones. The company observes that the Auto Scaling group launches more On-Demand Instances when end users access high volumes of static web content. The company wants to optimize cost. What should a solutions architect do to redesign the application MOST cost-effectively?

options.A: Update the Auto Scaling group to use Reserved Instances instead of On-Demand Instances.
options.B: Update the Auto Scaling group to scale by launching Spot Instances instead of On-Demand Instances.
options.C: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to host the static web content from an Amazon S3 bucket.
options.D: Create an AWS Lambda function behind an Amazon API Gateway API to host the static website contents.

explanations.A: Reserved Instances reduce cost but do not address the root issue of EC2 scaling for static content.
explanations.B: Spot Instances can reduce compute cost but still require EC2 scaling for static content, which is inefficient.
explanations.C: CloudFront with Amazon S3 offloads static content delivery to edge locations, reducing EC2 load and significantly lowering cost.
explanations.D: Using Lambda and API Gateway for static content introduces unnecessary request-based costs and higher operational expense.
explanations.correct: Serving static content from Amazon S3 through CloudFront is the most cost-effective and scalable approach.

questions.text: A company stores several petabytes of data across multiple AWS accounts and uses AWS Lake Formation to manage its data lake. The data science team wants to securely share selective data with the engineering team for analytics with the least operational overhead. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Copy the required data to a common account and grant cross-account IAM access.
options.B: Use the Lake Formation permissions Grant command in each source account.
options.C: Use AWS Data Exchange to privately publish the data.
options.D: Use Lake Formation tag-based access control to grant cross-account permissions.

explanations.A: Copying data increases storage cost and operational complexity.
explanations.B: Granting permissions individually in each account increases administrative overhead.
explanations.C: AWS Data Exchange is designed for data publishing and adds unnecessary complexity for internal sharing.
explanations.D: Lake Formation tag-based access control provides centralized, scalable, and secure cross-account data sharing with minimal overhead.
explanations.correct: Tag-based access control is the most efficient and secure way to share selective data across accounts.

questions.text: A company wants to host a scalable web application accessed by users worldwide. Users upload and download unique data up to gigabytes in size. The team wants a cost-effective solution to minimize latency and maximize performance. What should a solutions architect do?

options.A: Use Amazon S3 with Transfer Acceleration to host the application.
options.B: Use Amazon S3 with Cache-Control headers to host the application.
options.C: Use Amazon EC2 with Auto Scaling and Amazon CloudFront to host the application.
options.D: Use Amazon EC2 with Auto Scaling and Amazon ElastiCache to host the application.

explanations.A: S3 Transfer Acceleration optimizes long-distance data transfers for large, unique objects using AWS edge locations.
explanations.B: Cache-Control headers do not improve upload performance or latency for unique content.
explanations.C: CloudFront caching is ineffective for unique, non-cacheable uploads.
explanations.D: ElastiCache does not optimize large file uploads or downloads.
explanations.correct: S3 Transfer Acceleration is purpose-built for high-throughput global data transfers of large objects.

questions.text: A company has 700 TB of data on an on-premises NAS system and a 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect link. The company must migrate the data within 90 days without disruption and still access and update the data during transfer. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Use AWS DataSync to transfer the data to Amazon S3.
options.B: Use AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices.
options.C: Use rsync over the Direct Connect connection.
options.D: Back up the data to tape and ship it to AWS.

explanations.A: AWS DataSync efficiently transfers large datasets over Direct Connect while allowing ongoing access and updates.
explanations.B: Snowball Edge requires physical shipment and does not support continuous access during transfer.
explanations.C: Rsync lacks optimization, monitoring, and scalability for large enterprise migrations.
explanations.D: Tape-based migration causes significant disruption and long restore times.
explanations.correct: AWS DataSync is designed for large-scale, non-disruptive hybrid data migrations.

questions.text: A company runs an application with one Amazon RDS DB instance and two manually provisioned EC2 web servers in a single Availability Zone. A DB deletion caused 24 hours of downtime. What should a solutions architect do to maximize reliability?

options.A: Delete one EC2 instance and enable termination protection on the other.
options.B: Enable Multi-AZ and deletion protection for RDS and use an Auto Scaling group with an ALB across multiple AZs.
options.C: Use AWS Lambda with API Gateway and multiple DB instances.
options.D: Use Spot Instances with CloudWatch alarms and Multi-AZ subnets.

explanations.A: Reducing EC2 capacity decreases availability and does not address HA.
explanations.B: Multi-AZ RDS with deletion protection and EC2 Auto Scaling across AZs provides high availability and fault tolerance.
explanations.C: This adds complexity and does not prevent DB deletion issues.
explanations.D: Spot Instances improve cost efficiency, not reliability.
explanations.correct: A Multi-AZ architecture with load balancing and Auto Scaling maximizes infrastructure reliability.

questions.text: A company is deploying a two-tier web application in a VPC. The web tier is using an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group with public subnets that span multiple Availability Zones. The database tier consists of an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance in separate private subnets. The web application reports that it cannot connect to the database. The database is confirmed to be up and running. All configurations for the network ACLs, security groups, and route tables are still in their default states. What should a solutions architect recommend to fix the application?

options.A: Add an explicit rule to the private subnet’s network ACL to allow traffic from the web tier’s EC2 instances.
options.B: Add a route in the VPC route table to allow traffic between the web tier’s EC2 instances and the database tier.
options.C: Deploy the web tier's EC2 instances and the database tier’s RDS instance into two separate VPCs, and configure VPC peering.
options.D: Add an inbound rule to the security group of the database tier’s RDS instance to allow traffic from the web tier's security group.

explanations.A: By default, network ACLs allow all inbound and outbound traffic. Since the configurations are in their default states, the NACL is not blocking the traffic.
explanations.B: Within a VPC, all subnets can route traffic to each other by default via the local route. No additional routes are needed for communication between subnets in the same VPC.
explanations.C: VPC peering is unnecessary as both tiers are already in the same VPC. This would introduce significant operational overhead and complexity without addressing the root cause.
explanations.D: The default security group for a VPC allows all outbound traffic but blocks all inbound traffic except for traffic from the same security group. To allow the web tier to communicate with the RDS instance, an inbound rule must be added to the RDS security group specifically allowing traffic on the MySQL port (3306) from the web tier's security group.
explanations.correct: In AWS VPC architecture, Security Groups act as stateful firewalls. The default state for a security group is to deny all inbound traffic. Therefore, explicitly allowing traffic from the web tier to the database tier at the security group level is the required step.

questions.text: A company has a large dataset for its online advertising business stored in an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance in a single Availability Zone. The company wants business reporting queries to run without impacting the write operations to the production DB instance. Which solution meets these requirements?

options.A: Deploy RDS read replicas to process the business reporting queries.
options.B: Scale out the DB instance horizontally by placing it behind an Elastic Load Balancer.
options.C: Scale up the DB instance to a larger instance type to handle write operations and queries.
options.D: Deploy the DB instance in multiple Availability Zones to process the business reporting queries.

explanations.A: RDS Read Replicas allow you to offload read-intensive workloads (like reporting) from the primary DB instance. This ensures that the primary instance's resources are dedicated to write operations, improving overall performance.
explanations.B: RDS DB instances (except for Aurora) cannot be placed behind an Elastic Load Balancer for horizontal scaling in this manner. ELBs are used for web/app tiers, not for standard RDS MySQL scaling.
explanations.C: Scaling up (vertical scaling) might provide more resources, but the reporting queries would still compete with write operations for the same CPU and I/O resources on the single instance.
explanations.D: Multi-AZ deployments are designed for high availability and disaster recovery. The standby instance in a standard Multi-AZ deployment cannot be used for read/write operations; it only serves as a failover target.
explanations.correct: Read Replicas are the standard AWS architectural pattern for separating read-heavy reporting workloads from primary transactional write workloads in relational databases.

questions.text: A company maintains a searchable repository of items in an Amazon RDS for MySQL database with 10 million rows and 2 TB of General Purpose SSD storage. Insert operations are taking 10 seconds or longer due to storage performance issues. Which solution addresses this performance issue?

options.A: Change the storage type to Provisioned IOPS SSD.
options.B: Change the DB instance to a memory optimized instance class.
options.C: Change the DB instance to a burstable performance instance class.
options.D: Enable Multi-AZ RDS read replicas with MySQL native asynchronous replication.

explanations.A: Provisioned IOPS (PIOPS) SSD storage is designed to deliver fast, predictable, and consistent I/O performance. For a database experiencing slow inserts due to I/O bottlenecks on General Purpose (gp2/gp3) storage, upgrading to io1/io2 is the direct fix.
explanations.B: Memory-optimized instances provide more RAM, which helps with query processing and caching, but the question explicitly states that the bottleneck is 'database storage performance'.
explanations.C: Burstable instances (T-series) provide baseline performance with the ability to burst, which is unsuitable for high-volume, consistent workloads and would likely degrade storage performance further once credits are exhausted.
explanations.D: Read replicas offload read traffic. They do not improve the write performance (inserts) of the primary database instance; in fact, they can slightly increase primary load due to replication overhead.
explanations.correct: When the bottleneck is identified as storage I/O, the solution is to increase the available IOPS. Provisioned IOPS SSD allows for specific performance targets to be met regardless of volume size.

questions.text: A company hosts a three-tier ecommerce application on a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The instances run in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). All ecommerce data is stored in an Amazon RDS for MariaDB Multi-AZ DB instance. The company wants to optimize customer session management during transactions. The application must store session data durably. Which solutions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.A: Turn on the sticky sessions feature (session affinity) on the ALB.
options.B: Use an Amazon DynamoDB table to store customer session information.
options.C: Deploy an Amazon Cognito user pool to manage user session information.
options.D: Deploy an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster to store customer session information.
options.E: Use AWS Systems Manager Application Manager in the application to manage user session information.

explanations.A: Sticky sessions (session affinity) bind a user's session to a specific EC2 instance. This is not a 'storage' solution and fails the durability requirement because if the specific EC2 instance fails or terminates during an Auto Scaling event, the session data is lost.
